workouts.name: Regenerative spin 30 minutes
workouts.goal: Active rest day: loosens up the legs without tiring you
workouts.description: Half an hour of very easy riding in zone 1 (below 55% FTP), for the day after a hard workout or a race. Active recovery gets the circulation going without adding new load, so here less is more: if you feel tempted to speed up, get off early instead. Conversational pace, higher cadence, zero effort.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: Start with almost no load.

messages.text: Do not rush the rhythm; this warm-up is only about loosening up the legs.
Recovery is today's goal: the movement is what counts, not the watts.

steps.name: Easy spin
steps.note: Loose, round pedalling; if you could not talk, it is too hard.

messages.text: You are halfway: keep the upper body relaxed and do not hunch your shoulders.
One more minute of this, then we wind down slowly.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Just freewheel now, and let your neck and shoulders go.
Nice work; you did not have to work hard today, and that counts in training too.

workouts.name: Regenerative spin with bursts 45 minutes
workouts.goal: Recovery and loose pedalling technique at the same time
workouts.description: Three quarters of an hour in zone 1, with four one-minute high-cadence bursts (105–110 rpm) at the same easy wattage. The bursts keep the nervous system awake and polish round pedalling, while the load stays regenerative throughout. Ideal for the day between two key sessions.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: This is only the warm-up; today's goal is looseness. Keep your shoulders relaxed and do not grip the bars.

steps.name: Easy 1
steps.note: Loose riding, calm breathing.

messages.text: The first easy section is here: the watts are low, and the goal now is freshening up and staying loose.

steps.name: Spin 1
steps.note: The same easy watts, just faster legs; your saddle should not bounce under you.

messages.text: You are on the right track; the short bursts have loosened your legs. Now just hold the easy rhythm.
One more short burst, then the longer easy section follows. Keep the watts the same.
Eight minutes of the same easy pace. If your thighs feel heavy, simply slow down a little.
One more minute, then the cool-down. Enjoy this section, because this is where the recovery comes from.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Nice work; today's session served your rest. Now let your heart rate down slowly and breathe deeply.

workouts.name: Easy spin-out 60 minutes
workouts.goal: A longer active rest after a race or a hard block
workouts.description: An hour at the top of zone 1 and the bottom of zone 2 (50–55% FTP), when your body no longer asks for complete rest but is not ready for quality work yet. Its aim is to gently stimulate circulation and metabolism; you should feel fresher at the end than at the start. For more experienced riders, a lighter day in the weekly load.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: No chasing watts today; the goal is recovery. Feel your legs turning easily.

steps.name: Easy 1
steps.note: Steady and loose; do not raise the watts even when it feels easy.

messages.text: Keep this pace conversational: if breathing is already hard, back the watts off.
Five more minutes of this block. Keep your shoulders down and your collarbone relaxed.

steps.name: Easy 2
steps.note: Slightly faster legs, the same easy feeling.

messages.text: The legs spin faster now, but your heart rate must stay just as calm.
Last minute of this block. Let the cadence slow down by itself.
This is the third easy block already. Loosen your hands on the bars and breathe deeply.
Halfway. Take a sip and check whether your breathing is still easy.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: In the cool-down your job is to keep pedalling comfortably and not jump off abruptly.
Nice work; recovery is work too. Drink water and stretch at the end.

workouts.name: Beginner endurance 45 minutes
workouts.goal: Your first regular aerobic sessions, getting used to continuous riding
workouts.description: A short, steady zone 2 session for beginners or after a long break. Zone 2 (56–75% FTP) develops the aerobic capacity of the heart and muscles while you recover from it quickly, which is why it is the foundation of a training plan. When this feels easy, the 60-minute version is the next step.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: The warm-up prepares you for the longer steady work; let your legs warm up slowly.
Today's goal is getting used to continuous riding, not speed.

steps.name: Steady 1
steps.note: A calm pace; continuous nose breathing should just about work.

messages.text: The real work starts now; find the calm, even rhythm.
You are halfway; watch your breathing and do not tense your hands on the bars.

steps.name: Steady 2
steps.note: A hair stronger, but still a conversational pace.

messages.text: You can lift it a little now, but keep the cadence around 90; do not rush.
The last steady section is here, six minutes; after that only the easy part is left.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: You held on beautifully; this was your first real endurance session, and that is a big thing.

workouts.name: Beginner endurance 60 minutes
workouts.goal: Building up to an hour of continuous zone 2 riding
workouts.description: An hour of steady aerobic work with the load lifted gently twice and then brought back. For beginners this is the weekly base session: it improves fat and carbohydrate metabolism, capillary density and the number of mitochondria. Keep the pace conversational throughout; the goal is time in the saddle, not watts.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: The warm-up prepares you for today's hour of work. The aim is for your breathing to stay calm throughout.

steps.name: Steady 1
steps.note: A loose, steady pace.

messages.text: The longer steady part is here. Make sure your legs turn in an even, round motion.
Find the rhythm: cadence around 90, shoulders loose, hips quiet in the saddle.

steps.name: Lifted 1
steps.note: A little more decisive, breathing still calm.

messages.text: You give a little more now, but you could still talk. This is the right pace; this is how it should feel.
Back to the base level. This part builds the foundation of long endurance; no need to push.
Take a few sips; longer work needs fluid. Check your posture while you drink.
The last lifted section is here. Hold the cadence and keep your shoulders from tensing.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: You rode a full hour nicely. Now let your breathing and heart rate settle slowly.

workouts.name: Base endurance 75 minutes
workouts.goal: Continuous zone 2 work, aerobic efficiency
workouts.description: The classic base session: long, steady blocks in the middle of zone 2. Both the pros and the research (the polarized training model) show that most of the weekly load is spent at this easy-to-moderate pace, because it builds the most aerobic base with the least fatigue. Watch out for heart rate drift: if it creeps up at steady watts, drink and do not push.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: This base session is about zone 2: a comfortable pace, no need to prove anything.

steps.name: Zone 2 – 1
steps.note: Steady watts, loose upper body.

messages.text: If your breathing turns ragged, ease off a little; the goal now is staying power.
Five more minutes, then the upper part of the zone. Until then, keep the cadence even.

steps.name: Zone 2 – 2
steps.note: The upper part of the zone, still controlled.

messages.text: The pace is a little stronger now, but keep your shoulders and arms loose on the bars.
Last minute of this block; do not let your hips rock over the saddle.
Back down into the easier part of zone 2; keep the pedalling smooth and round.
Halfway; a little water helps now. Two or three sips, then back to the rhythm.
Two more minutes, then the cool-down. Keep the pedalling round to the end.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Now the easy riding is what matters; the stretching comes later.
Nice base work; your aerobic base grew again today. Drink and relax.

workouts.name: Base endurance 90 minutes
workouts.goal: Building the aerobic base with a longer, stable load
workouts.description: An hour and a half of zone 2, with a fifteen-minute section at the top of the zone in the middle. Because of the length, glycogen stores and fuelling matter now: eat and drink every 30–45 minutes, the way you would in a race. One of the most important base sessions; worth putting in once or twice a week.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: We are warming up the engine now; before the long work, let your legs get used to the rhythm.
A few more minutes, then the long, steady zone 2 section comes.

steps.name: Zone 2 – 1
steps.note: Calm, steady work; eat something in the middle of the block.

messages.text: The rhythm is there, your legs are used to the load; now just hold it.
Halfway: sit up straight, stretch a little and take a sip.
One more minute of this, then we close a little looser.

steps.name: Zone 2 upper
steps.note: The top of the zone, but still not tempo.

messages.text: You work a hair harder now, but the exhale should be long and calm.
Three more minutes of this, then back to the easier pace.
The last big block is here: thirty minutes of steady zone 2 work.
Over this length small faults grow; check your shoulders and the position of your head.
Last minute of the block; after that only the cool-down is left.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: That was nice, long work; your aerobic base is a little stronger now.

workouts.name: Base endurance 2 hours
workouts.goal: Long aerobic work indoors, with cadence changes against monotony
workouts.description: Two hours in zone 2, with the cadence alternating in twenty-minute sections (85–95) so that the long indoor session does not become monotonous and your pedalling improves too. Long, easy work is the most important stimulus for mitochondrial adaptation and fat use. It needs 60–80 g of carbohydrate an hour and regular drinking.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Today's two hours are long, steady work. Just warm up now and find the comfortable rhythm.

steps.name: Zone 2 – 1
steps.note: We change cadence section by section; the watts stay in zone 2 throughout.

messages.text: In the first quarter of an hour keep your breathing deep and even, and your heart rate calm.
Take a few sips now; two hours need both fluid and energy.
Five minutes are left in this block; your legs are still holding up well.
Second block: the watts are a little higher, the cadence around 90. The same calm breathing.
Five more minutes, then the next cadence change. Until then, watch your posture.
Long, steady work: the higher 95 cadence freshens your legs; do not chase the watts.
Halfway through the whole session. Watch your posture now, and do not hunch over the bars.
You ride with slower legs and more force, but keep your heart rate in zone 2.
Take another sip and check that your shoulders are not tensing up.
The last big block. Hold your breathing and your posture; sit quietly in the saddle.
Five minutes and this is over too, then the cool-down. You are holding up well; this is long endurance.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Two hours of riding are in your legs; that is a serious base. Now let your heart rate down slowly and stretch.

workouts.name: Long base session 150 minutes
workouts.goal: Long-term aerobic load and lasting endurance
workouts.description: Two and a half hours of steady zone 2, with short lifted sections. The long base session builds not only aerobic capacity but durability: how much your power drops after hours. Current research says this is one of the best predictors of race results, amateurs included. Fuel regularly.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: This is your longest base session, so the pace matters now, not the speed.

steps.name: Zone 2 – 1
steps.note: Steady; eat and drink every 30 minutes.

messages.text: In the first quarter of an hour let your legs get used to the long load; do not rush.
Now is the time for some carbohydrate and water, before the fatigue arrives.
Two more minutes, then the upper zone. Keep your cadence the same.

steps.name: Zone 2 upper
steps.note: The upper part of the zone.

messages.text: The pace is noticeably stronger, but your breathing is still controlled and even.
Halfway through the block: let your shoulders drop and do not squeeze the bars.
Last minute of this block; ease the pace back a little now.
Back down to the easier pace; keep the pedalling smooth and round.
Two or three sips of water help now, and roll your neck and shoulders.

steps.name: Zone 2 upper 2
steps.note: Keep the quality at the end too: round pedalling, loose shoulders.

messages.text: You are in the middle of the last block: keep your form so you do not fade by the end.
The last minute of the longest base session; only this one minute is left.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: This multi-hour base was serious work. Just freewheel now and enjoy the calm.

workouts.name: Long base session 180 minutes
workouts.goal: The longest indoor base session, maximum aerobic volume
workouts.description: Three hours in zone 2: the indoor version of the long weekend ride. The sections undulate gently within the zone, and at the end you have to hold on at the top of the zone when you are already tired; that is the durability workout. Only worth starting with a proper base, plenty of food and plenty of fluid.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: This long session is about aerobic volume; let the warm-up be patient.
Three more minutes, then the first long zone 2 block.

steps.name: Zone 2 – 1
steps.note: Steady; eat and drink every 30 minutes.

messages.text: The rhythm settles now; keep the cadence around 90.
Halfway: keep your shoulders loose and low, and your exhale long.
Last minute of the block; the next section will be a little stronger.
Forty minutes of steady work follow; now it is about staying power.
Halfway; let your feet relax, do not squeeze the pedals, and pedal rounder.
One more minute of this; make the next block just the same.
Third long block, the same calm pace; now your attention is what matters.
Halfway; take a sip and check that your shoulders are not tensing.
One minute left of this; do not slow down abruptly at the end.

steps.name: Tired upper zone 2
steps.note: You are tired already: the same quality, steady watts, a calm upper body.

messages.text: Pedal the same way now too, and keep your knee in line with the pedal.
Ten minutes are left of this; now only staying power is needed.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: You rode almost three hours; that is an incredible aerobic base to build on later.

workouts.name: Cadence drill 60 minutes
workouts.goal: Pedalling technique and a wide cadence range
workouts.description: An easy zone 2 session alternating high (around 110) and low (around 60) cadence sections at the same easy wattage. The aim is not force but coordination: round pedalling without jerks at every cadence. A useful technique session for beginners and in the base period too.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Today's session is about cadence: for an hour we alternate the pedalling rhythm so your legs learn every range.

steps.name: Steady 1
steps.note: Base cadence, loose riding.

messages.text: A cadence of 90 is the reference now. Remember this rhythm, because the next sections build on it.

steps.name: High cadence 1
steps.note: Fast legs; keep the hips quiet in the saddle.

messages.text: The fast section is in the middle. Work only from the ankle and the knee; keep the upper body loose.
Back to the base cadence. Notice the difference in your legs between the fast and the slower rhythm.
Second fast section. Hold the revs, but do not let the watts rise above what is needed.
Now slow back down to 88 and relax your hands on the bars.

steps.name: Low cadence 1
steps.note: Push through the whole circle, not just down.

messages.text: Slow legs, high force. Make sure your knee does not jerk and your hips stay stable.
After the harder part we return to the easier rhythm. Breathe deeply and let the tension go.
Last slow block. The same technique: a full circle, a calm upper body, and do not yank the bars.
Five minutes are left of the last steady section, then the cool-down.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: You rode a full hour, which is nice work for your feel for cadence. Now spin on slowly and breathe deeply.

workouts.name: Base ride with sprints 90 minutes
workouts.goal: Building the aerobic base while keeping your sprint sharp
workouts.description: An hour and a half of zone 2 with six short 10-second sprints, each followed by a good five minutes of easy riding. Short maximal sprints barely tire you, yet they keep the nervous system and the fast muscle fibres awake even in base weeks. In the sprints the trainer is in free mode: as many watts as you can push at full effort.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: The warm-up prepares you for the sprints: let your legs get thoroughly warm, because short sprints come soon.

steps.name: Zone 2 – opening
steps.note: Steady zone 2.

messages.text: This is a pace at which you could still chat; hold it.
A little over a minute, then the first sprint. Start watching your cadence.

steps.name: Sprint 1
steps.note: Ten seconds at full effort; start standing, then sit back down.

steps.name: Zone 2 – 1
steps.note: For the first minute spin very loosely, then back into zone 2.

messages.text: After the sprint let your breathing slow; keep the watts in zone 2.
Second sprint done. Back to zone 2 now, and let your breathing slow.
Third sprint done. Sit back in the saddle and hold the zone 2 pace.
After the fourth sprint you are halfway: two sprints more, then the closing block.
Last sprint done; the longer closing zone 2 block comes. Breathe deeply.
Halfway through the closing block; breathe loosely and let your heart rate slow.
Last minute of the closing block; keep the cadence even.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Nice work; you got both the sprints and the base. Slow down and drink water.

workouts.name: Upper zone 2 3 × 20 minutes
workouts.goal: Work around the aerobic threshold (LT1), higher aerobic power
workouts.description: Three twenty-minute blocks at the top of zone 2 (72–75% FTP), just below the aerobic threshold. The Norwegian method also does large volumes of controlled work at this boundary: hard enough to give a significant aerobic stimulus, but not yet accumulating lactate, so you can train again the next day. Keep your breathing calm throughout; if you cannot even talk, it is too hard.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Today's session is work around the aerobic threshold; the warm-up prepares you for it.
Two and a half minutes, then the first tempo block.

steps.name: Upper zone 2 1
steps.note: 72–75% FTP, below the boundary; keep it conversational to the end.

messages.text: The rhythm is there; keep the cadence around 90 and your exhale long.
Five more minutes; make sure the pace does not creep up towards the end.

steps.name: Rest 1
steps.note: Five minutes easy; drink.

messages.text: Stretch now and relax your shoulders before the next block.
Second block, twenty minutes below the threshold, the same pace as the first.
Halfway; check your posture and do not let your upper body tip forward.
One minute left; keep the cadence even all the way.
The second rest comes, five minutes easy, then the last block.
The last twenty minutes come; the pace is the same, so do not burn yourself at the start.
Halfway; keep your breathing deep and rhythmic, your legs calm.
The last minute, and then only the easy part is left.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: You did three blocks; this work around the threshold builds your aerobic power.

workouts.name: Base session with a tempo finish 2 hours
workouts.goal: Durability: holding tempo on tired legs at the end of a long session
workouts.description: After an hour and a half of zone 2, twenty minutes of tempo (85% FTP), then a cool-down. Races are decided at the end, when hours are already in your legs; the gap between fresh and tired performance (durability) can be trained on its own, and research says it separates successful amateurs from the rest well. In the tempo block the watts must not drop.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: At the end of today's long work you have to hold tempo on tired legs, so do not burn your energy now.

steps.name: Zone 2 – 1
steps.note: Steady; eat regularly, you need the energy at the end.

messages.text: Ten minutes of the block have passed. Check your hands: are they tiring on the bars?
Twenty minutes have passed, halfway through the block. Adjust your posture and do not hunch over the bars.
Ten minutes until the next block; keep your heart rate calm until then.
Second long block. You will feel the fatigue here, but keep the watts the same.
This block is the base part: your legs are used to the rhythm, just hold it.
Twenty minutes are left in this block; your legs are still fresh.
Ten minutes until the tempo, so save your energy now.

steps.name: Tired tempo
steps.note: Twenty minutes of tempo at the end of the long work: steady, no more.

messages.text: The middle of the section comes: despite the tired legs, hold 85% and do not speed up.
Five minutes left; now it only takes discipline. Do not jerk the pace.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Two hours of work are behind you. Now ease off slowly and breathe deeply.

workouts.name: Tempo 3 × 15 minutes
workouts.goal: Muscular endurance and aerobic power in zone 3
workouts.description: Three fifteen-minute tempo blocks (78–82% FTP) with five minutes of rest. Tempo is the intensity of flat riding on the road, of long climbs and of group riding: hard enough to strengthen muscular endurance, but well below threshold. A good entry into structured intervals and into the second half of the base period.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Today's three tempo blocks are in zone 3; start spinning easily in the warm-up.

steps.name: Tempo 1
steps.note: Decisive but controlled; you could only speak in short sentences.

messages.text: In zone 3 your breathing should be powerful but still controlled.
Five minutes left; do not let the tempo slow towards the end.
Rest: relax your shoulders, but keep the cadence turning; do not stop.
Second tempo block. The same watts and the same breathing; do not speed up at the start.
Halfway through the second block; keep your trunk stable and do not let your hips rock.
Last minute of the second tempo; only this one minute is left.
Rest: take a sip and watch how your breathing comes down.
The last tempo block comes; now your head has to hold on.
Halfway through the third block; keep your legs round and your hands loose.
One more minute, then the cool-down. Just a little more.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Three tempo blocks are behind you; that is serious work. Ease off slowly now.

workouts.name: Tempo 2 × 40 minutes
workouts.goal: Long, steady tempo endurance
workouts.description: Two forty-minute tempo blocks: the pace of long sportives and gran fondos, indoors. Long, steady zone 3 work develops muscular endurance and durability, and teaches you to fuel under load. For advanced riders at the end of the base period or preparing for a long race.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Today's session is about long tempo endurance; the warm-up prepares you for it.
Five minutes left, then the first big tempo block starts.

steps.name: Tempo 1
steps.note: Steady; drink every 15 minutes.

messages.text: The tempo settles now; keep the cadence around 88 and your legs moving loosely.
Halfway; sit up straight, do not hunch your shoulders, and watch your breathing.
Last minute of the first block, then a short rest.
A short rest comes; relax and get ready for the second, even more tired block.
Five more minutes, then we start again; check your posture.

steps.name: Tempo 2
steps.note: The same quality when more tired; that is the point.

messages.text: The fatigue comes now, but keep your feet calm and do not squeeze the pedals.
Halfway; stretch a little and drink, so the second half stays strong.
Ten minutes left; keep the tempo even, do not think about sprinting.
One more minute, then the cool-down; the hardest part is behind you.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: You rode almost two hours; this long tempo builds your staying power, and you did it very well.

workouts.name: Tempo pyramid
workouts.goal: A gradual tempo load with changing block lengths
workouts.description: Five tempo blocks that grow longer and then shorter (5-10-15-10-5 minutes), with the intensity rising from the bottom of the zone to the top. The changing length develops your sense of pace and piles up almost 45 minutes of zone 3 work without monotony. For the second half of the base period.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Halfway through the warm-up. Today's pyramid gets harder step by step; for now just wake your legs up.

steps.name: Tempo 5′
steps.note: The bottom of the zone.

messages.text: This is the first short tempo: you are still fresh, so keep it even and do not sprint the start.
Rest, but do not stop. Ride easily and exhale long.
The ten-minute tempo comes now. Look for a stable feeling; your legs and your breathing should be in tune.
You are halfway through the ten-minute block. Keep your breathing deep and controlled.
Three minutes of rest. Check your heart rate and take a sip.

steps.name: Tempo 15′
steps.note: The top of the pyramid: steady, disciplined.

messages.text: Halfway up the top: shoulders loose, hips quiet, the pace unchanged.
Five minutes are left of the hardest block. Do not ease off; this section gives the most.
Four minutes of rest, but keep the pedals turning; do not let your legs stop.
The second ten-minute tempo. The fatigue is there already, so keep the cadence around 86.

steps.name: Tempo 5′ (2)
steps.note: The last, strongest tempo.

messages.text: This is the pyramid's strongest short block. Keep a little reserve in you at the end.
Thirty seconds more; give what is left, then the work is over.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: After an hour of tempo this easy part feels good. Bring the pace down slowly and give yourself credit for the work.

workouts.name: Tempo 1 × 60 minutes
workouts.goal: An hour of continuous tempo: aerobic power and mental endurance
workouts.description: A single one-hour tempo block at 78–82% FTP, which can also be done in a time-trial position. Long, uninterrupted work trains concentration, holding the position and even pacing, not just the aerobic system. An advanced base session, before long races and time trials.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Today's task is staying power: set the rhythm of your breathing in the warm-up.

steps.name: Tempo 60′
steps.note: Steady watts, a calm upper body; drink every 15 minutes, but do not leave the position.

messages.text: The first minutes are decided in your head; do not speed up, just hold 80%.
Check your shoulders: if they have crept up, drop them and breathe deeper.
You are halfway, and now your head is the harder part, not your legs.
Twenty minutes left; keep the pace the same and your breathing steady.
Ten minutes left; the hardest mental part comes now.
Last minute of the tempo. Sit up straight and hold on a little longer.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: You held tempo for a whole hour; that is a big achievement. Slow down now.

workouts.name: Tempo 3 × 15 minutes with accelerations
workouts.goal: Holding tempo through repeated changes of rhythm
workouts.description: Three tempo blocks with a 15-second acceleration at 140% every three minutes, then straight back into tempo. In a bunch you can rarely ride evenly: picking the tempo up again after surges and clearing lactate on the move can both be trained. Belongs in the first weeks of the build period, the antechamber of threshold work.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: This warm-up prepares you for the tempo and the accelerations; let your legs warm up slowly.
Four minutes, then the first tempo block; keep the cadence around 88.

steps.name: Tempo 1/1
steps.note: Tempo; between accelerations go back to the same watts.

messages.text: First round; let the tempo be comfortably hard and keep your breathing deep.

steps.name: Acceleration 1/1
steps.note: Fifteen seconds sharply, seated or standing.

messages.text: Five minutes easy now; let your breathing calm down and take a sip.
Second set; after every acceleration go back to the same watts.
You are halfway through the second set; keep the tempo the same and do not break away in the acceleration.
Second rest; relax and get ready for the last, third set.
Third set; your legs are tiring, but after the accelerations go back into tempo just the same.
Last round; keep the tempo the same, the final acceleration comes at the end.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Three sets, fifteen accelerations in all; that trains tempo endurance. Well done.

workouts.name: Sweet spot introduction 4 × 8 minutes
workouts.goal: The first step into sub-threshold work, with short blocks
workouts.description: Four eight-minute blocks at 85–88% FTP with four minutes of rest. Sweet spot (88–94% FTP) sits between tempo and threshold: a lot of training effect for relatively little fatigue. This introductory version with short blocks shows you what the zone feels like before you switch to the longer 12–20 minute repetitions.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: This is your first time at sub-threshold work. Do not tire yourself out in the warm-up; save energy for the blocks.

steps.name: Sweet spot 1
steps.note: Strong but sustainable; at the end you should still feel you had a fifth one in you.

messages.text: Halfway through the block. Hold 87%, keep your breathing deep and your shoulders down.
Four minutes of rest follow. Do not sit up; spin easily and relax your hands.
Second block. The same tempo as the first; do not count on your initial momentum.
Three minutes are left, and keep your cadence around 90.
A little air and a sip. The third block will be closer to the threshold.
Third block. This is when the temptation to speed up is greatest. Do not.
Two minutes left. Bring the steady tempo; do not rush the end.
The last sweet spot block. From now on the fatigue comes, but keep the watts the same.
Two minutes left; keep the pedalling steady.
Thirty seconds, then the cool-down.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: You did four blocks; this is the foundation of sub-threshold work. Now ease off slowly and breathe calmly.

workouts.name: Sweet spot quick 2 × 12 minutes
workouts.goal: Efficient threshold work when you only have 45 minutes
workouts.description: Two twelve-minute sweet spot blocks after a short warm-up. Sweet spot is popular because it gives a big training stimulus per unit of time, so it is meaningful, quality work even in a tight schedule. Ideal as a weekday session during the base and build periods.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Sweet spot is sub-threshold but still substantial work. The warm-up now prepares your legs.

steps.name: Sweet spot 1
steps.note: 88–90% FTP, evenly; make the second block just the same.

messages.text: This is neither a sprint nor a rest but constant pressure on the pedals; hold it.
Two more minutes, then the rest. Keep your form; do not tire your hands.
Rest: shake out your legs, take a sip, then the second block comes.
Second block: the same watts as the first. Do not run ahead with the pace.
You are halfway; your legs know the rhythm now, keep it even.
Last minute; watch that your hips stay quiet, then the cool-down comes.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: The work is done; the sweet spot settles in nicely now. Relax and stretch a little.

workouts.name: Sweet spot 3 × 12 minutes
workouts.goal: Raising FTP with moderate fatigue
workouts.description: Three twelve-minute blocks at the bottom of the sweet spot with four minutes of rest: the first sweet spot session of most training plans. 36 minutes of sub-threshold work in all, from which you can still recover well the next day. When this feels easy, move on to the 2 × 20 or the 3 × 20 minute version.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: The warm-up prepares you for the sweet spot, that is, for strong but manageable work.
Two minutes, then the first twelve-minute block; get ready.

steps.name: Sweet spot 1
steps.note: A strong, steady tempo; breathing deep but rhythmic.

messages.text: Halfway; keep the cadence around 90 and do not let the momentum speed you up.
One minute left; do not relax at the end, hold the watts.
Relax now; before the second twelve minutes let your breathing settle.
Second block, the same tempo as at the start; do not rush the beginning.
One more rest, then the third and last sweet spot.
The last twelve minutes; despite the fatigue, work on the quality.
Two minutes left; at the end put everything into the tempo.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Three strong blocks are behind you; this work gives a lot to your FTP too.

workouts.name: Sweet spot 2 × 20 minutes
workouts.goal: Long, continuous sweet spot work
workouts.description: Two twenty-minute blocks in the middle of the sweet spot (90–92% FTP). The twenty-minute repetition is one of the basic forms of threshold development: long enough for the muscles to work under sustained load, but not as taxing as real threshold work. Once or twice a week at the end of the base period and in the build period.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: This is today's two twenty-minute effort; save energy in the warm-up. Wake your legs up slowly.

steps.name: Sweet spot 1
steps.note: Steady; do not push too hard in the first five minutes.

messages.text: The tempo is in the upper part of the sweet spot now. Look for a stable feeling and do not jump ahead.
Ten minutes have passed, ten more to go. Keep your cadence around 90.
Five minutes are left of the first block. Keep your shoulders loose and your breathing controlled.
Five minutes of rest. Drink and get ready for the second twenty-minute block.

steps.name: Sweet spot 2
steps.note: The same discipline; the second block is where the session's value lies.

messages.text: Second twenty-minute block. The first went well; carry on the same way, do not push harder.
Ten minutes are left of the steady work. Do not let your heart rate jump; hold the pace.
The last three minutes: you can hold the tempo a little longer at the end; do not ease off.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Two twenty-minute blocks; sweet spot work is valuable. Now ease off slowly and breathe deeply.

workouts.name: Sweet spot 3 × 20 minutes
workouts.goal: High-volume sweet spot, race endurance
workouts.description: An hour of sweet spot in three blocks: one of the most effective ways to raise threshold power and lasting force once 2 × 20 is easy. The third block starts on tired legs, so it develops durability too. Drink during the rests, and take carbohydrate during the blocks as well.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Before this high-volume work do not tire yourself; spin loosely so your legs warm up.

steps.name: Sweet spot 1
steps.note: 90% FTP, evenly; the last block goes at the same wattage too.

messages.text: A twenty-minute block: deliberately hold back in the first minutes so you still have strength at the end.
Halfway through the first block; keep your breathing rhythmic, not ragged.
Last minute of the first block; the tempo is the same, get ready for the short rest.
Rest: drink and relax your hands, but keep the pedals turning.
Second twenty minutes: keep your hips and shoulders quiet, the watts the same.
Ten minutes have passed; do not raise the watts, just hold them.
Last minute of the second block; only this one minute is left.
Rest: loosen your collarbone, look ahead; the third block comes.
The last twenty minutes come; your head knows the rhythm now, and so do your legs.
Ten minutes left; no need to speed up, only to hold.
Last minute of the race-endurance block; hold the rhythm to the end.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Three big sweet spot blocks are behind you; that is race endurance. Relax, you can be proud.

workouts.name: Sweet spot 1 × 45 minutes
workouts.goal: Continuous strength endurance in the sweet spot
workouts.description: Three quarters of an hour without a break at the bottom of the sweet spot: the mental and physical dress rehearsal for long time trials and climbs. Continuous work also practises holding the position and pacing. For advanced riders, once 3 × 15 and 2 × 20 minutes are confident.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: The warm-up prepares you for the 45-minute block, which is long but controlled work.
Seven minutes left, then the big block starts; keep your breathing calm.

steps.name: Sweet spot 45′
steps.note: Steady watts, a calm upper body; the first ten minutes should feel easy.

messages.text: The rhythm is there; keep the cadence around 88 and your legs moving loosely.
In a block this long keep your attention on your breathing, not on the power.
Halfway; shoulders loose, trunk straight, head calm.
Fifteen minutes left; do not accelerate at the end, the same tempo is needed.
Seven minutes are left of the block; this is when many people start to squeeze, so you relax.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: That was nice, even work; this is exactly what the sweet spot builds.

workouts.name: Progressive sweet spot 25 + 24 minutes
workouts.goal: A gradual load increase within the zone, sense of pace
workouts.description: Two long blocks in which the watts rise slowly: the first from 84 to 89%, the second from 88 to 94%. Because of the gradual rise it is easy to stay disciplined at the start, while at the end you work at the top of the zone, already tired. A good choice if you tend to start intervals too hard.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Halfway through the warm-up. Watch the cadence now; the progressive blocks get harder step by step.

steps.name: Progressive block 1
steps.note: The trainer raises it slowly; you just follow.

messages.text: Hold 84% at the start and do not try to give more. You will still have strength at the end.
Ten minutes are left of the first block; the watts are close to 89 now.
Two minutes left. Breathe deeply and keep the cadence to the end.
Four minutes of rest. It is not comfortable, but you will need fresh legs for the second block.

steps.name: Progressive block 2
steps.note: The end of the block is the top of the zone; hold the cadence.

messages.text: This block starts higher, so watch your breathing, not the clock.
You are in the middle of the block. Your legs may tire, but keep your posture and breathing good.
Two minutes left. No need to save anything now; give it everything at the end.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Two sustained blocks; your sense of pace improves a lot with this. Now loosen your legs and bring your heart rate down.

workouts.name: Sweet spot 4 × 10 minutes with cadence changes
workouts.goal: Sub-threshold work and cadence flexibility
workouts.description: Four ten-minute sweet spot blocks, each at a different cadence (90, 72, 100, 85). Holding the same wattage at different revs demands different muscle work and coordination, just like varying terrain. It adds a technical stimulus to threshold development, without monotony.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Today's session plays with cadence: try the different revs during the warm-up.

steps.name: Sweet spot 1 (90)
steps.note: Natural cadence.

messages.text: Look for the comfortable rhythm here; it will be the reference for the other blocks.
Rest: relax, and get ready to work at a slower cadence in the next block.

steps.name: Sweet spot 2 (72)
steps.note: Lower revs, more torque; keep the upper body loose.

messages.text: Slow revs, more force: do not let your knee turn out, and keep your ankle quiet.
Rest: the next block will be fast; relax your hands and shoulders.

steps.name: Sweet spot 3 (100)
steps.note: Fast legs; do not let the hips rock.

messages.text: Fast revs; your breathing will get quicker, which is normal, so keep the 89% power.
Before the last block take a few sips and loosen your hands.
Last sweet spot block: the natural cadence is fine, but the watts are what matter.
Halfway; hold the 89% watts, no need to change the cadence any more.
Last minute; your legs are ready, just a little more.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Four blocks, four different cadences; that was nice work. Relax now and see how much you learned.

workouts.name: Sweet spot over-under
workouts.goal: Lactate clearance and handling changes of intensity below the threshold
workouts.description: Two eighteen-minute blocks alternating three minutes at 88% with one minute at 95–97%. The short “over” sections produce a little lactate, and in the “under” sections you have to clear it while still riding; that is the ability you need when the pace of the bunch surges and eases. A gentler antechamber to the over-unders around the threshold.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Today's session is about changing intensity; the warm-up now prepares the legs.
Four minutes, then the first set; watch the changes.

steps.name: Under 1/1
steps.note: Under: the bottom of the sweet spot, where you clear the lactate.

messages.text: In the first round the change is what matters; cadence around 88 and do not let the pace slip.

steps.name: Over 1/1
steps.note: Over: just below FTP; noticeably stronger, but not frantic.

messages.text: You are in the middle of the first set; keep your breathing long and the changes identical.
Five minutes easy; stretch and get ready for the second, harder set.
Second set; the easier parts are still hard now, but keep the pace the same.
Halfway through the second set; keep your exhale strong and do not rush.
Last stronger section; give it everything, but keep the cadence around 95.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: You went through twelve changes; this builds your lactate tolerance, and you did it nicely.

workouts.name: Sweet spot with short surges
workouts.goal: Sweet spot load with sharp, short accelerations
workouts.description: Three sets in which three minutes of sweet spot are followed by a 20-second acceleration at 115–118%, then straight back into the sweet spot. The accelerations imitate the jumps that happen in a bunch; the point is that the watts must not drop after them. In the build period, a more race-like version of plain sweet spot.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Halfway through the warm-up. Short, sharp accelerations come today, so let your legs be warm.

steps.name: Sweet spot 1/1
steps.note: Sweet spot, evenly.

messages.text: Halfway through the block. Keep your breathing deep and your hands from tensing on the bars.

steps.name: Surge 1/1
steps.note: Twenty seconds sharply, then straight back into the sweet spot.

messages.text: Four minutes of rest. Relax, do not stop, and get ready: the second set will be harder.
Second set. After the first your legs know the rhythm; do not race the start.
The second half of the second set comes. The surges now come on more tired legs; keep your breathing strong.
Second rest, then the last set. Drink and stretch your back.
Third and last set. Now you have to hold around 90%, and the surges get stronger.
The last sweet spot block; after it only one surge is left. Keep the cadence.
Thirty seconds are left, then the last surge. Get ready.
The last surge. Start standing, at full effort, and after that only the cool-down.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Three sets, many surges: you worked seriously for this. Let your heart rate come down slowly.

workouts.name: Threshold 2 × 20 minutes
workouts.goal: Load close to FTP, developing the lactate threshold
workouts.description: The classic threshold session: two twenty-minute blocks at 95–98% FTP with five minutes of rest. The aim is to push the lactate threshold higher under a long, steady load and to get used to the discomfort of a time trial or a long climb. If the watts drop by more than 5% and stay there, end the block.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: In threshold work the warm-up is key: feel your legs, because strong work comes soon.

steps.name: Threshold 1
steps.note: Steady tempo, controlled breathing.

messages.text: At the threshold your sentences should be short; that is a good sign if it feels that way.
Halfway: stay at 97%, keep your upper body calm.
Last minute of the first block; get ready for the short rest.
Rest: take a sip and loosen your shoulders; the second block comes.

steps.name: Threshold 2
steps.note: The same watts; the second block is the more important one.

messages.text: You are halfway; your legs may tire, but keep your breathing controlled.
Last minute; hips stable, collarbone relaxed.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Two twenty-minute threshold blocks; that was serious work. Slow down now and stretch.

workouts.name: Threshold 2 × 30 minutes
workouts.goal: Long, steady threshold load for sustainable FTP
workouts.description: Two half-hour blocks below the threshold (93% FTP): extending your time at threshold, that is, how long you can hold a pace close to FTP. One of the most specific sessions for riders preparing for time trials and long climbs. Only once 2 × 20 minutes at 95% is confident.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: The warm-up prepares you for the threshold; let your legs warm up slowly.
Eight more minutes, then the first thirty-minute threshold block starts.
Two minutes left; your breathing should be rhythmic by now.

steps.name: Threshold 1
steps.note: The first ten minutes should feel easier than they should.

messages.text: Sit up straight, shoulders loose, and keep the tempo even at 93 percent.
Halfway; stretch on the bars and check that your exhale is long.
Five minutes left; do not let momentum speed you up, hold the watts.
Last minute; do not collapse at the end and do not surge forward.
Five minutes of rest; just relax and get ready for the second threshold.

steps.name: Threshold 2
steps.note: Position, breathing, steady watts.

messages.text: Second block; the fatigue comes now, but keep the cadence around 86.
Halfway; keep your posture and make the exhale long and strong.
This is when most people slow down; you hold the pace and do not lose your exhale.
One minute and the hard part is over; hold it all the way.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: That was the threshold's two big blocks; let your legs loosen slowly now.

workouts.name: Threshold 3 × 15 minutes
workouts.goal: 45 minutes of threshold work, raising how long you can hold FTP
workouts.description: Three fifteen-minute blocks at 97–100% FTP: 45 minutes at the threshold in all, which is more work than 2 × 20 minutes. The last block is slightly stronger so there is still a challenge at the end. In the build period, preparing for a time trial or long climbs.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Halfway through the warm-up. Today's three threshold blocks are long, so just wake your legs up.

steps.name: Threshold 1
steps.note: 97% FTP, evenly.

messages.text: Halfway through the first block. Keep your breathing rhythmic and your shoulders loose.
Two minutes are left of the first threshold block; the hardest part comes now.
Five minutes of rest. Drink, loosen your shoulders, and get ready for the second threshold.
Second threshold block. The same tempo as the first; do not race the start.
Halfway through the second block. Your legs may be tired, but keep the watts the same.
Five minutes of rest. Use your breathing to bring the heart rate down a little.

steps.name: Threshold 3
steps.note: The last block at FTP.

messages.text: Halfway through the third block. You come to this one already tired, so keep your breathing deep.
Two minutes and the last threshold is done. Give it everything, but keep your form.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Three big threshold blocks; beautiful persistence. Ease off slowly now and look back proudly.

workouts.name: Threshold 4 × 10 minutes
workouts.goal: Shorter, repeated threshold blocks for holding high watts
workouts.description: Four ten-minute blocks at FTP with four minutes of rest. Because the blocks are shorter, 40 minutes of threshold work accumulate at a higher intensity than in a 2 × 20. A good transition between the sweet spot and the long threshold blocks, and an excellent maintenance session in the race period too.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: At the end of the warm-up feel your legs; this is the base of today's FTP work.

steps.name: Threshold 1
steps.note: At FTP; do not overshoot in the first minute.

messages.text: Halfway; press evenly, and do not start accelerating in your head.
Rest: shake out your legs and drink; the next block will be just as strong.
Second block: the same watts as the first. Do not try for more.
Halfway. Watch only the next minute; nothing else matters now.
Before the third block relax your hands and keep your shoulders down.
Third threshold block: your head works now, your legs are used to it.
Halfway through the third; hold the rhythm, and your sentences should still be short.
The last block comes; loosen your shoulders, you will need it.

steps.name: Threshold 4
steps.note: The last block a hair above FTP.

messages.text: Halfway through the last block; hold the extra watts, keep your breathing controlled.
Last minute: you can give everything now, but keep your form.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Four threshold blocks; that was nice work. Slow down now, and the stretching can come.

workouts.name: Threshold ladder 3 × 12 minutes
workouts.goal: A gradually rising threshold load within the blocks
workouts.description: Three twelve-minute blocks in which the watts rise from 92% to 100–104%. You start in the sweet spot and finish above FTP, so you have to hold the biggest load when tired, like at the top of a climb. The blocks start higher each time.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Today's session is a rising threshold load; let the warm-up heat your legs.
Five minutes left; the load will rise slowly.

steps.name: Step 1
steps.note: The trainer raises it slowly; the last minutes are what matter.

messages.text: Calm breathing at the start, cadence around 90, and do not jerk the pedals.
Halfway; the load is higher already, but keep your posture straight.
Half a minute left; breathe deeply and keep the rhythm.
Rest; after the first step let your breathing settle, then the second comes.
The second step starts on tired legs; do not blow up at the start.
Halfway; the tempo is at FTP now, keep the exhale long.

steps.name: Step 3
steps.note: The last step takes you above FTP.

messages.text: Third step; your legs are tired, but keep your breathing calm.
Two minutes left; do not ease off at the end, this is the most important part.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Three steps, each one higher; that was real threshold work, and you did it nicely.

workouts.name: Over-under 3 × 5 rounds (112% / 90%)
workouts.goal: Developing on-the-move lactate clearance around the threshold
workouts.description: Three sets of five rounds each: one minute at 112% (over), then two minutes at 90% (under). The over section accumulates lactate, and in the under section you have to clear it below the threshold but still under load. This is the ability you need after an attack, or when the steeper parts of a climb give you no rest either.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Halfway through the warm-up. Today's over-under blocks practise lactate handling; wake your legs up.

steps.name: Over 1/1
steps.note: Over: one minute above FTP, with momentum.

messages.text: During the first over: keep the cadence above 95 and your breathing strong.

steps.name: Under 1/1
steps.note: Under: do not rest; clear the lactate below the threshold.

messages.text: Halfway through the under: breathe long; breathing helps break down the lactate.
Four minutes of rest after the first set. Drink, relax your hands, and bring your heart rate down.
Halfway through the second set. The under follows the over, so do not stop now.
Second rest, then the third set, the hardest part. Breathe deeply.
The last set. The same rhythm as before, but your legs will be more tired.
Last over, with momentum. Keep your breathing powerful but do not let the cadence drop.
The last under. After it only the cool-down follows; hold the pace to the end.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: After three over-under sets this cool-down is deserved. Bring the watts down slowly and breathe deeply.

workouts.name: Long over-under 2 × 20 minutes
workouts.goal: Twenty-minute over-under blocks, race-like threshold load
workouts.description: Two twenty-minute blocks alternating 90 seconds at 110% with one minute at 92%. On average you are close to FTP, but the constant changes of rhythm are far more race-like than an even 2 × 20. For advanced riders, in the second half of the build period.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Today brings a varying load: spin loosely but with focus during the warm-up.

steps.name: Over 1/1
steps.note: Over: 110%, with momentum, but not like a sprint.

messages.text: A short but strong section; at 110% your breathing will get quicker, which is completely normal.

steps.name: Under 1/1
steps.note: Under: 92%, no resting here either.

messages.text: We are in the middle of the first block. Lead the changes with your breathing now, not with your legs.
The first block's last over comes; show what you can still take.
The last under in the first block, then five minutes of rest.
Five minutes of rest: drink, loosen your shoulders; the second block asks for the same attention.
Second block; your legs know the rhythm now, so plan the changes around your breathing.
Halfway through the second block: the changes are harder now, but breathing helps.
Our last over comes; put in what you have and keep your form.
The last under, just this one minute, then the cool-down.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: After two over-under blocks, big work is behind you. Slow down and stretch.

workouts.name: Threshold 3 × 12 minutes with accelerations
workouts.goal: Threshold work with twenty-second accelerations, race-like changes of rhythm
workouts.description: Three twelve-minute threshold blocks with a 20-second acceleration at 120% every 160 seconds. After the accelerations you have to settle back onto the threshold without the watts dropping; that is what you need after a breakaway or an attack on a climb. A hard key session, before the race period.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: The warm-up prepares you for the race-like changes of rhythm; let your legs warm up now.
Five minutes left; the short accelerations come after the first threshold block.

steps.name: Threshold 1/1
steps.note: At FTP, evenly.

messages.text: First round; keep the pace stable, and raise the cadence to 90 before the acceleration.

steps.name: Acceleration 1/1
steps.note: Twenty seconds sharply, then back to the threshold.

messages.text: First set done; let your breathing settle, the second set will be harder.
Second set; after the accelerations back to the threshold, do not ease off.
Halfway through the second set; keep the cadence around 90 and do not rush after the acceleration.
Second set done; relax a little, there is time to breathe before the last set.
Third set; the tempo is 98 percent, keep your breathing calm.
Last acceleration; give everything for twenty seconds, then back to the tempo.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Three sets, many accelerations; that trains your ability to hold the threshold. Well done.

workouts.name: Tired threshold, pre-fatigued
workouts.goal: Holding threshold power after pre-fatigue
workouts.description: Ten minutes above FTP, then three fifteen-minute blocks at a falling but still high intensity (96–94%). A tired body learns to hold watts, which is decisive in the final of a race; research says durability is a trainable ability of its own. For advanced riders, tuning up for a race.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Halfway through the warm-up. A strong pre-fatigue comes first, so do not waste your legs now.

steps.name: Pre-fatigue
steps.note: Ten minutes above the threshold; you are still fresh here.

messages.text: Halfway through the pre-fatigue. Do not rush it, but keep the watts even.
One minute left of the pre-fatigue; now just hold on.
Three minutes of rest. The tired threshold follows, so breathe deeply.

steps.name: Tired threshold 1
steps.note: Hold the watts, even when it feels hard.

messages.text: Halfway through the first tired block. Keep your breathing strong and rhythmic; your body is tired already.
Two minutes are left of the first tired block; hold the watts for now.
Three minutes of rest, and you still feel tired. That is normal; get ready for the next block.
The second tired block. If it feels hard, keeping the cadence around 86 makes it easier.
Halfway through the second tired block. The watts will not get easier, only more even.
Rest comes now: drink and get ready for the third, hardest block.

steps.name: Tired threshold 3
steps.note: The last block is decided in your head.

messages.text: Halfway: keep your breathing and posture stable, and do not hunch your shoulders.
Two minutes left; put every bit of strength here.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: After a hard session this cool-down feels good. Let your heart rate down slowly and look back at how much you held.

workouts.name: Seiler 4 × 16 minutes
workouts.goal: Long threshold intervals following the protocol of the Seiler trial
workouts.description: Four sixteen-minute blocks with two minutes of rest at the highest intensity still sustainable evenly (on average ~95% FTP in the trial). Seiler et al. (2013) compared it with the 4 × 8 and 4 × 4 minute versions: all three improved, the long blocks mainly the threshold power. A large volume of controlled threshold work, once 3 × 15 minutes is routine.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: This is the Seiler protocol: long, controlled blocks. Let the warm-up not tire you.

steps.name: Threshold 1
steps.note: The highest pace still sustainable evenly; do not let it be decided in the first block.

messages.text: Feel the 95%: it can be held for a long time, so do not add extra watts.
Four more minutes, then a short rest. Do not ease off now.

steps.name: Rest 1
steps.note: Two minutes of rest: short, but enough for a sip.

messages.text: Drop your shoulders and watch your breathing slow down.
Second block, the same watts. Hold the rhythm deliberately now.
Halfway through the second block: keep your upper body calm and your wrists loose.
Relax a little and watch how your heart rate comes down.
Third block: this is the test, but the pace stays the same.
Six more minutes, then a short rest, and the last block comes.
Halfway through the last block; now you only have to hold to the end.
Last minute; do not speed up, just hold 95% to the end.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Four sixteen-minute threshold blocks; that was serious work. Slow down now and calm down a little.

workouts.name: Norwegian threshold 5 × 8 minutes
workouts.goal: Controlled threshold work, a lot of quality time with little fatigue
workouts.description: Five eight-minute blocks at 92–94% FTP with only one minute of rest. The essence of the Norwegian method is to do threshold work deliberately below the threshold, broken up with short rests, so a large volume accumulates without recovery taking days. At the end of the session you should feel you still had more in you.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: The Norwegian method is controlled work; the warm-up now prepares your legs.
Five minutes left; the set comes after the first eight-minute block.

steps.name: Threshold 1
steps.note: Just below the threshold; if it keeps getting harder, it is too strong and badly paced.

messages.text: Halfway; keep the cadence around 90 and your breathing rhythmic.
One minute left; do not give up the pace.

steps.name: Rest 1
steps.note: One minute easy, no more.

messages.text: Second block; start it just like the first, with a calm but persistent pace.
This is the middle block; the most important thing now is calm, even pedalling.
Rest after the third block; let your breathing settle, the next one comes.
Fourth block; your legs are tired, but keep the control.
Last block; give what strength is left, but keep the pace.
Two minutes left; hold on a little longer at the end.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Five blocks; this is the Norwegian method, your staying power works well, and you did it very well.

workouts.name: Norwegian threshold 10 × 3 minutes
workouts.goal: Shorter, slightly stronger threshold sections with a short rest
workouts.description: Ten three-minute sections at 96–98% FTP with one minute of rest. After the pattern of the shorter and slightly quicker afternoon dose of a Norwegian double threshold day: the short sections let the time spent at the threshold grow without the lactate running away. 30 minutes of work close to FTP with less load than a traditional 2 × 15.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Halfway through the warm-up. Today's ten short threshold blocks come; just warm your thighs now.

steps.name: Threshold 1
steps.note: A hair below FTP; the tenth should not be a struggle either.

messages.text: Halfway through the first three-minute block. Keep your breathing deep and regular.

steps.name: Rest 1
steps.note: One minute of easy spinning.

messages.text: Half a minute, then the next block. Breathing is the most important thing now; do not let your hands tense.
Second block. The short rest is only there to air out your legs; do not relax too much.
Halfway through the set. Your heart rate is high already, but keep the cadence around 92; that is the key.
Eighth block. Your legs are tired, but keep the cadence constant.
The last, tenth block. After it only the cool-down; give it everything.
A minute and a half left; let your breathing drive the pace now.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Ten short threshold blocks; that was one of the hardest parts of the whole session. Ease off slowly now.

workouts.name: Threshold quick 3 × 8 minutes
workouts.goal: A quality threshold stimulus in 45 minutes
workouts.description: Three eight-minute blocks at FTP with three minutes of rest, after a short but thorough warm-up. When time is short, threshold work still works: 24 minutes at FTP maintains and develops the threshold. A good key session for a weekday evening.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Short but intense work comes; feel your legs during the warm-up.

steps.name: Threshold 1
steps.note: At FTP, evenly.

messages.text: Halfway through the first eight minutes; keep your breathing rhythmic.
Last minute; use your head now, keep the revs and the watts.
Three minutes of rest: drink and get ready for the second eight minutes.
Second block with the same watts. Now the pace has to be held in your head.
Halfway through the second block; keep your shoulders loose and your hands calm.
The last block comes, and the same watts again. Sit comfortably.
Halfway through the last block; deep breathing helps now, and do not let your legs slow down.
One more minute; watch only the end now, then the cool-down.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Three eight-minute threshold blocks; nice work. Slow down now and stretch.

workouts.name: Threshold time extension 1 × 40 minutes
workouts.goal: Holding a pace close to FTP for as long as possible
workouts.description: A single forty-minute block at 94% FTP: the most specific session for time trials and long climbs. Raising time to exhaustion, that is, making threshold power not only higher but holdable for longer, can be trained on its own. For advanced riders only, those confident with 2 × 20 minutes.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Before the forty-minute threshold block, the warm-up now prepares your legs.
Five minutes left; get ready so the pace stays even.

steps.name: Threshold 40′
steps.note: The first twenty minutes should be restrained; the second half shows what your sense of pace is worth.

messages.text: Your exhale is there; keep the cadence around 88 and your shoulders loose.
Twelve minutes; keep your breathing rhythmic and your head calm.
Twenty minutes, halfway; do not let the pace speed up now, check the cadence.
Ten minutes left; do not speed up towards the end, staying power is what matters now.
Last minute; do not give in at the end, but keep the pace the same.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Forty minutes at the threshold; this builds your ability to hold a pace close to FTP, and you did very well.

workouts.name: VO2max 4 × 4 minutes (Helgerud)
workouts.goal: Raising VO2max and the heart's pumping capacity
workouts.description: Four four-minute intervals at 90–95% of maximum heart rate (about 110–115% FTP) with three minutes of active rest. In the trial by Helgerud et al. (2007) this format raised VO2max the most, with a rise of about 10% in stroke volume. A simple, easily repeated, very effective aerobic key session.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Today's protocol is 4 × 4 minutes. The warm-up is the key now; open up your breathing.

steps.name: VO2max 1
steps.note: Climb up during the first minute, then hold it; by the end your breathing should be maximal.

messages.text: Halfway through the first interval. Do not watch the heart rate, watch your breathing: deep, strong, even.
Forty seconds left; now just hold on, give it everything.

steps.name: Rest 1
steps.note: Three minutes of active rest, easy riding.

messages.text: Halfway through the rest. Take a sip and get ready for the second interval to be just as strong.
Second four minutes. Keep the same cadence and force as the first.
Second rest. Your legs are still full of energy; do not sit still.
Third interval. The fatigue is at its greatest now, but breathing is the key.
The last four minutes. Even if your breathing is hard now, keep the cadence around a hundred.
A minute and a half left; just hold on, you will still have a little strength at the end.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Four big intervals; you worked seriously for this. Ease off slowly and breathe deeply.

workouts.name: VO2max 5 × 5 minutes
workouts.goal: Maximum oxygen uptake with longer VO2max repetitions
workouts.description: Five five-minute intervals at 108–112% FTP with five minutes of rest. The five-minute repetition is long enough for several minutes of each block to spend near VO2max. A good choice once 4 × 4 is going and you want more work in the high aerobic range.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Five five-minute VO2max blocks come; focus on your legs at the end of the warm-up.

steps.name: VO2max 1
steps.note: Hard but even; it should get really hard in the fourth minute.

messages.text: Halfway through the first block: keep the revs around 100 and do not slow down.
Last minute; you can take this much more, keep the revs around 100.
Five minutes of rest: breathe, relax your hands, the next block comes.
Second block: do not overshoot in the first minute; you need the extra at the end.
Rest: take a sip and loosen your hips.
Third block. Work with deep breathing, not ragged gasps.
Rest before the fourth block; your heart rate drops, but your legs are still fresh.
The harder minute comes now: your head whispers to stop, but keep the revs.
Last five minutes: everything into the revs, keep your hands calm.
Halfway through the last block; hold the revs, there will be time to relax at the end.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Five five-minute VO2max blocks; that was big work. Slow down now and stretch a little.

workouts.name: VO2max 6 × 3 minutes
workouts.goal: A VO2max stimulus with shorter, repeatable sections
workouts.description: Six three-minute repetitions at 118% FTP with four minutes of rest. The shorter repetition allows a higher intensity, so you reach VO2max sooner, and the rest is still enough to keep the quality. A good middle ground between 4 × 4 and micro-intervals.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Six short, strong sections come; the warm-up now prepares your heart.
Seven minutes left; before the first big round keep your breathing deep.

steps.name: VO2max 1
steps.note: A strong start, then hold it; the last minute is what matters.

messages.text: First round; the 118 percent pace should not be frantic, cadence around 102.
Thirty seconds more; do not ease off, keep the pace the same.
First round done; in the rest let your breathing settle before the second round.
Second round, the same force as at the start; keep the breathing deep now.
You are halfway, in the middle of the third round; keep your legs spinning and your upper body calm.
Two rounds are left; relax now and drop your shoulders.
The last round, the sixth; make this the strongest pace you can still hold.
One more minute; push at the end too, do not ease off.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Six rounds; that was the VO2max work, your heart and your legs both worked, very good.

workouts.name: VO2max 8 × 2 minutes
workouts.goal: VO2max and practising the fast rise in breathing
workouts.description: Eight two-minute repetitions at 120% FTP with three minutes of rest. Because the repetitions are short they are manageable for beginners and in the race period too, yet 16 minutes of work accumulate in the high aerobic range. It also prepares you for short climbs and breakaways.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Halfway through the warm-up. Today's eight short hard sections train your breathing, so relax now.

steps.name: VO2max 1
steps.note: Two minutes hard; breathing rises fast, that is the point.

messages.text: The middle of the first two-minute section. You will be gasping; that is normal, keep the cadence at 104.
Three minutes of rest; keep pedalling easily, that makes the next hard section easier too.
The second two minutes. After the short start hold the pace; do not stamp too suddenly.
Halfway, the fifth hard two minutes. Keep your breathing controlled, not ragged.
Two hard two-minute sections are left. Relax now and bring your heart rate down.
Seventh section. One more at the end, so do not run out of strength.
The last hard section. Keep your breathing controlled and the cadence up all the way.
Thirty seconds left; put everything in.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Eight hard two-minute sections; that is serious VO2max work. Bring the pace down slowly and breathe deeply.

workouts.name: VO2max 10 × 1 minute
workouts.goal: Tolerating short, repeatable high intensity
workouts.description: Ten one-minute repetitions at 125% FTP with two minutes of rest. The one-minute sections work at the boundary of VO2max and the anaerobic system, so they prepare you well for criteriums, short climbs and attacks. In the second half every repetition takes you close to VO2max.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Ten short, hard minutes come; do not waste your legs in the warm-up.

steps.name: VO2max 1
steps.note: One minute hard, seated; even, not a sprint.

messages.text: Your heart rate rises fast, but keep the revs and the pace the same.
Two minutes of rest: shake out your hands and take a deep breath.
Four done, the fifth comes now, five more after it.
Five done, the sixth comes now, four more after it.
Seven done, three are left. Take a deep breath; your legs still hold.
The last minute: pull everything out of yourself, keep the revs around 105.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Ten hard minutes; that was real performance. Slow down now and drink water.

workouts.name: Billat 30/30 – 3 × 10
workouts.goal: A long time near VO2max with micro-intervals
workouts.description: Thirty seconds of hard work (about maximal aerobic power, ~120–125% FTP), thirty seconds of easy rest, in three sets of ten. According to Billat's studies, the 30/30 alternation lets you spend more time near VO2max with less lactate than continuous, very hard work. It should only get really hard by the end of a set.

steps.name: Warm-up
