steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: The thirty-second rhythm is fast; the warm-up now prepares your heart rate.
Five minutes left; keep your breathing calm, the first short section comes.

steps.note: Thirty seconds sharply, but not maximally; hold the same pace throughout.

steps.name: Easy
steps.note: Thirty seconds easy; do not stop.

messages.text: Halfway through the first set; keep the cadence around 100 and do not slow down.
The last short section of the first set; give out the pace at the end too.
The first set is done; in the rest let your breathing settle, then the second comes.
Halfway through the second set; during the 30 seconds keep your knee in line.
The last short section of the second set; give out the pace once more.
Second set done; after the rest the third and last comes.
Third set; cadence and pace the same as at the start.
Last short section; put every last bit here, then only the cool-down.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Three sets, many short strong sections; that was serious VO2max work, nicely done.

workouts.name: VO2max 40/20 – 3 × 8
workouts.goal: Loading VO2max and anaerobic capacity together
workouts.description: Forty seconds of work at 120% FTP, twenty seconds of rest, in three sets of eight. Because the rest is short, oxygen uptake does not fall back, so in the second half of a set you work near VO2max throughout. Harder than the 30/30; for advanced riders, before the race period.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.
Forty seconds hard, evenly.

messages.text: Twenty seconds left; keep your breathing strong and the cadence high.

steps.name: Easy
steps.note: Twenty seconds: relax, but keep the legs turning.

messages.text: Fourth interval, halfway through the first set. Keep your legs spinning and your shoulders loose.
The last interval of the first set. Give it everything; a short rest follows.
Five minutes of set rest. Drink, relax your back, and get ready for the second set.
Two minutes left; breathe deeply and bring your heart rate down.
The first interval of the second set. The same pace as the first; do not rush it.
Halfway through the second set. Keep your breathing controlled and the cadence high.
The last interval in the second set. Give everything, then only the rest comes.
Five minutes before the last set. Take a sip and watch your breathing.
The third set, the last one. Ride just as before; your legs know the rhythm.
The last interval of the whole session. Come on, this is the final forty seconds.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Three sets, eight intervals each. After the VO2max work bring your heart rate down slowly.

workouts.name: Rønnestad 30/15 – 3 × 13
workouts.goal: Power between VO2max and threshold, a research-proven format
workouts.description: Three sets of thirteen rounds each: 30 seconds of work (about 118–125% FTP), 15 seconds of easy riding; three minutes of rest between sets. In Rønnestad et al.'s studies this short-interval format produced bigger gains in peak power and in the 20-minute test than long 4 × 5 minute intervals at the same load. The aim is the highest wattage you can hold through all three sets.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Three sets come, each with 13 short repetitions. Do not tire yourself in the warm-up.

steps.note: Thirty seconds strong, but so that the third set still works.

steps.name: Easy
steps.note: Fifteen seconds easy.

messages.text: Six done in the first set, the seventh comes now. Six repetitions are left.
The last repetition of the first set. Hold it even once more, then three minutes of rest.
Three minutes of rest: sit up straight, take a deep breath and drink.
Second set, the same rhythm. Keep the revs around 100 at the start.
Halfway through the second set: your breathing is quick, but keep the rhythm.
The last repetition in the second set. Do not ease off at the end, then the rest.
Three minutes of rest before the last set. Drink and open up your chest.
The middle of the last set, six repetitions are left; keep the revs.
This is the last repetition; give it everything, then the cool-down.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Thirty-nine hard repetitions; that was nice work. Slow down now and relax your hands.

workouts.name: Rønnestad 30/15 introduction – 2 × 10
workouts.goal: Getting to know the 30/15 format with shorter sets
workouts.description: Two sets of ten 30/15 rounds (30 seconds at ~118% FTP, 15 seconds easy) with three minutes of rest. A lighter, shorter introduction to the 3 × 13 protocol used in the research: it teaches pacing before you do the full version. A serious aerobic stimulus even in a short time.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: The warm-up prepares you for the 30/15 rhythm; let your legs warm up slowly.
Four minutes left; keep your breathing calm before the first set.

steps.note: A strong, even 30 seconds; the first rounds should feel easy.

steps.name: Easy
steps.note: Fifteen seconds easy.

messages.text: Halfway through the first set; do not sit up in the 15-second rest, keep spinning.
The last round of the first set; keep the cadence around 100, do not slow down.
Three minutes of rest; let your breathing settle, the second set comes.
Second set; keep the cadence the same as at the start.
Last round; give the 30 seconds once more, then it is over.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Ten and ten rounds; this 30/15 format was a good introduction, nicely done.

workouts.name: Seiler 4 × 8 minutes
workouts.goal: A large volume of work just above the threshold – the winning protocol of the trial
workouts.description: Four eight-minute intervals with two minutes of rest at the highest intensity still holdable (on average ~105–106% FTP in the trial). In Seiler et al.'s (2013) seven-week study this group improved the most in VO2peak and in power at the 4 mmol lactate threshold, more than the 4 × 4 and the 4 × 16 minute groups. Its secret is a lot of hard but not maximal work.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Halfway through the warm-up. Today's four eight-minute intervals are above the threshold; raise the pace slowly now.

steps.name: Interval 1
steps.note: Hard but even; the fourth has to be finished at the same wattage.

messages.text: Halfway through the first eight minutes. Do not speed up; keep the cadence at 95.
One minute left of the first. Breathe strongly and keep the pace the same.

steps.name: Rest 1
steps.note: Two minutes of easy spinning.

messages.text: Second eight minutes. Hold the watts; do not watch the fatigue.
Halfway through the second interval. This is when it is easiest to overdo it, so keep the rhythm.
Two minutes of rest. Slow your breathing and take a sip.
Third interval. You are more tired, but the watts stay the same.
One more minute, then the rest.
The last eight minutes, the fourth interval. Your legs are tired, but your breathing is still controllable.
Halfway through the last interval. Concentrate on the end now.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Four eight-minute intervals above the threshold; you worked hard for this. Bring your heart rate down slowly.

workouts.name: Variable-intensity 5 × 8 minutes (Rønnestad 2024)
workouts.goal: More time near VO2max with long intervals of varying pace
workouts.description: Five eight-minute intervals, each starting with a 30/15 part (118% / 60%), then one-minute sections at 110% and 90% alternating; with two minutes of rest. Odden, Rønnestad et al. (2024) showed with 22 cyclists that the larger the share of oxygen uptake during the interval, the bigger the improvement in performance; a varying pace helps that. An advanced key session.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Five sets come with a varying pace. Wake your legs up during the warm-up.

steps.name: 1. – 30″ strong
steps.note: A hard start: it raises oxygen uptake quickly.

steps.name: 1. – 1′ up
steps.note: From here one-minute changes: up at 110%, down at 90%, do not rest.

messages.text: We are in the middle of the first set. The changes get harder now, but breathing helps.
The closing part of the first set. Carry it through with the revs, then two minutes of rest.
Two minutes of rest: take a sip, the second set will feel familiar.
Second set: you know the thirty-second effort now; keep the revs.
Halfway through the third set; the changes ask a lot of your legs now.
The closing part of the fourth set. Do not let the revs fall back; keep your attention.
Two minutes of rest before the last set. Take a deep breath and drink.
The last set; hold the revs as you reach the end, do not slow down.
Halfway through the last set; six sections remain, do not let your breathing fall apart.
Last section; give it everything, then the cool-down.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Five long sets with a varying rhythm; you held on very well. Slow down now and relax.

workouts.name: Variable-intensity VO2 6 × 5 minutes
workouts.goal: An interval that delivers a VO2max stimulus with less suffering
workouts.description: Six five-minute intervals alternating 30 seconds at 125% with 60 seconds at 100%, with two and a half minutes of rest. In Bossi et al.'s study, with variable-intensity work sections the cyclists spent more time above 90% of VO2max than with steady intervals of the same average, while the perceived effort was no greater.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: The variable-intensity blocks are about quick changes; the warm-up now prepares your legs.
Five minutes left; before the first peak keep your breathing calm.

steps.name: 1. – peak
steps.note: 30 seconds at 125%: lift your breathing.

steps.name: 1. – hold
steps.note: 60 seconds at FTP: do not rest, hold it.

messages.text: The pace is what matters now; keep the cadence around 92 and the exhale long.
The last peak of the first round; this is the strongest thirty seconds, then rest.
The first round is done; in the rest let your breathing settle, the second round comes.
Halfway through the second round; keep the pace around 92, do not ease off.
The last peak of the second round; keep the cadence at the end too.
The last peak of the third round; keep the cadence high, then you can relax.
Four rounds are behind you; in this rest loosen your shoulders and hands.
The last peak, the end of the sixth round; put all your strength in.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Six rounds at a varying pace; this VO2max stimulus works with less suffering, nicely done.

workouts.name: Hard-start VO2max 5 × 4 minutes
workouts.goal: A quicker rise in oxygen uptake, more time near VO2max
workouts.description: Five four-minute intervals: the first 45 seconds at 135%, then 3 minutes 15 seconds at 108%; with three minutes of rest. The hard start raises oxygen uptake faster, so a larger part of the interval is spent near VO2max; research says it is exactly this time that correlates with improvement. After the start do not try to accelerate further.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Halfway through the warm-up. This session is about the hard start; just wake your legs up.

steps.name: 1. – hard start
steps.note: 45 seconds very strong, seated; this is not a sprint.

messages.text: The first hard start; the initial impulse is what counts. Stay seated and keep the cadence at 105.

steps.name: 1. – hold
steps.note: Back to 108% and hold it; keep your breathing at its peak.

messages.text: Halfway through the hold. Keep your breathing deep and your cadence steady at 98.
Twenty seconds left; just hold the 108% now.
Three minutes of rest. After a hard start the breathing will be heavy; that is natural.
Second hard start. Seated the same way, a strong launch, but do not sprint.
Halfway through the five. After the initial impulse the hold must be disciplined.
The last hard start. After it only one hold section comes, and we do that too.
The last hold. Close the fifth block just like the first.
Forty-five seconds left; loose but strong.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Five hard starts and five holds; that was a hard session. Ease off slowly now and breathe deeply.

workouts.name: 15/15 micro-intervals 2 × 16
workouts.goal: A high aerobic load with short, easily paced sections
workouts.description: Two sets of sixteen rounds each, alternating 15 seconds at 125% with 15 seconds at 55%. With the 15/15 format Helgerud et al. (2007) also achieved significant VO2max gains, close to those of 4 × 4 minutes. The short sections are less intimidating, so it is a good choice for riders new to high intensity.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Two sets come, each of 16 short sections. Let the warm-up stay easy now.

steps.note: Fifteen seconds briskly, even, not a sprint.

steps.name: Easy
steps.note: Fifteen seconds easy; keep the legs turning.

messages.text: Seven done, the eighth comes now, eight are left. Do not over-accelerate.
The last repetition of the first set; keep your breathing controlled, then rest.
Five minutes of rest: drink, relax your hands, the second set follows.
Second set, the same rhythm, fifteen seconds briskly.
Halfway through the second set. The revs matter now, not the pressure.
The last repetition. Give out what is left, then the cool-down.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Thirty-two short hard sections; that was nice work. Slow down now.

workouts.name: VO2max pyramid 1-2-3-4-3-2-1
workouts.goal: Varied VO2max work with sections growing longer and then shorter
workouts.description: One-, two-, three- and four-minute sections, then three, two and one again, at 110–125% FTP (the shorter ones stronger), with rest as long as the work. The pyramid gives 16 minutes of work in the high aerobic range in all, and the changing lengths make it easier mentally too. For the middle of the build period.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: The pyramid alternates short and long sections; the warm-up now prepares your legs.
Five minutes left; before the first short section keep your breathing calm.

steps.name: 1 minute (1.)
steps.note: The shorter sections are stronger; the four-minute one is the top of the pyramid.

messages.text: Only one minute now, but hard; keep the cadence around 100.
Second section, two minutes at 120 percent; keep your exhale long.
Third section, three minutes; keep the pace even and do not surge forward.
Here is the top of the pyramid: cadence 100 for the four minutes, shoulders loose.
Halfway through the four-minute section; keep your breathing deep and do not grip the bars.
Now we come back down; the sections get shorter, but do not let the pace slip.
This is the two-minute section, then one last short, strong part comes.
Last section, one minute; give it everything, then the intervals are over.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: The pyramid was hard throughout; the sections built up nicely. Nice work.

workouts.name: VO2max quick 5 × 3 minutes
workouts.goal: A VO2max stimulus in 45 minutes
workouts.description: Five three-minute repetitions at 115% FTP with three minutes of rest, after a compact warm-up. A full-value VO2max session even when time is short: 15 minutes of work in the high aerobic range. A good weekday key session in the build and race periods.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: This short session is about the VO2max stimulus. Relax during the warm-up and get ready for the three-minute blocks.

steps.name: VO2max 1
steps.note: Three minutes hard; be at your peak by the third minute.

messages.text: Halfway through the first three-minute section. Your breathing is strong already, but keep the cadence at 100.
Thirty seconds left; give what is left.
The second three minutes. After the first you know how much reserve you have; do not start too hard.
Halfway. The third hard section is the biggest load; let your breathing steer it.
The fourth three minutes. One more is left; do not ease off.
The last three minutes. Give it everything; at the end only your breathing counts.
One minute left; just hold on now.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: After five hard three-minute blocks this cool-down is rest. Let your heart rate down slowly and give yourself credit.

workouts.name: VO2max introduction 6 × 2 minutes
workouts.goal: A first meeting with VO2max intervals
workouts.description: Six two-minute repetitions at 110% FTP with three minutes of rest. The short section and the generous rest make this the friendliest way into high-intensity work, yet it gives a real aerobic stimulus. When it feels easy, the 8 × 2 or Helgerud's 4 × 4 can follow.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: This is your first taste of VO2max. Wake your legs up for the revs in the warm-up.

steps.name: VO2max 1
steps.note: A strong but controlled two minutes; you do not have to get out of breath.

messages.text: Halfway through the two minutes; take a deep breath and hold 110%.
Three minutes of rest: drink and watch your breathing slow.
Second round, the same pace. Do not try to do more than in the first.
Two rounds done, the third comes now. Keep your revs around 98.
Fourth round: you may tire here, but keep your breathing and your revs even.
Four done, the fifth comes now, and one more after it.
Five done, the last round comes. Sit up straight and hold to the end.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Six two-minute VO2max rounds; nice work for a first meeting. Relax now and drink.

workouts.name: Anaerobic capacity 2 × 3 × 45 seconds
workouts.goal: Developing anaerobic capacity and lactate tolerance
workouts.description: Two sets of three near-maximal 45-second sections (about 150% FTP), with four minutes of rest and eight between sets. Efforts of 30–60 seconds need long rest so the quality holds throughout; this is not endurance training but capacity training. For attacks and short climbs.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Anaerobic work is short but intense; the warm-up now prepares your legs.
Five minutes left; before the first 45 seconds keep your breathing deep.

steps.name: Anaerobic 1/1
steps.note: A near-maximal 45 seconds; do not fall apart in the last ten seconds.

messages.text: Rest; let your breathing settle, because the next 45 seconds are what matter.
Second round, the same pace as at the start; do not rush now.
The last round of the first set; keep the cadence over the 45 seconds.

steps.name: Set rest
steps.note: Eight minutes of easy riding, a full reset.

messages.text: The first set is done; take a sip now and get ready for the second.
Second set; the 45 seconds need the same focus, do not blow up at the start.
Halfway through the second set; cadence around 100, shoulders loose.
The last 45 seconds; give everything at the end too, then the cool-down.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Two sets of three short, strong sections; your anaerobic capacity got a good workout.

workouts.name: Sprint intervals 6 × 30 s (Gibala)
workouts.goal: A big training effect in very little time
workouts.description: Six 30-second all-out (Wingate-style) sprints with four minutes of easy rest. In Gibala et al.'s experiments, 4–6 × 30 s sessions done three times a week produced muscle oxidative adaptations similar to several times as much endurance riding. In the sprints the trainer is in free mode: start from a high cadence and push to the end.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Today's six short sprints take little time, so the warm-up is the key now. Bring your heart rate up.

steps.name: Sprint 1
steps.note: 30 seconds all out; the watts will fall in the second half, that is natural.

messages.text: Ten seconds left; put everything in.

steps.name: Rest 1
steps.note: Four minutes of very easy riding.

messages.text: Halfway through the rest. Loosen your shoulders and slow your breathing.
Halfway through the six sprints. Your legs are tired, but the starting effort stays the same.
Two sprints are left. Relax a little and get ready.
The last sprint. Go at it full force, then the cool-down.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Six sprints, a big effort in little time. Bring your heart rate down slowly; nice work.

workouts.name: Anaerobic capacity 6 × 1 minute
workouts.goal: One-minute efforts: attacks, short climbs, finales
workouts.description: Six one-minute sections at 135% FTP with four minutes of rest. One-minute work loads anaerobic capacity and lactate tolerance, and the generous rest keeps every repetition quality. For criteriums, cyclocross and short, steep climbs.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: The short, very hard minutes come now. Sharpen your legs at the end of the warm-up.

steps.name: Anaerobic 1
steps.note: One minute very hard, evenly; do not burn it in the first 15 seconds.

messages.text: Halfway: your legs feel it, but keep the 135% going.
Four minutes of rest: sit, loosen your shoulders and take a sip.
The second minute, just like the first. Keep your leg speed high.
The third; you are halfway. Work with deep breathing and do not tense your neck.
The fourth comes; after it only two are left. Seated or standing, but keep the revs.
The fifth comes; after it only the sixth. Do not let the revs go.
The last minute; give it everything, there is room for a finish sprint at the end.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Six hard minutes; very nice work. Relax now and ride on slowly.

workouts.name: Sprint 8 × 10 s with full recovery
workouts.goal: Peak power and neuromuscular sprint capacity
workouts.description: Eight ten-second maximal sprints, each followed by five minutes of easy riding. Developing peak power needs full recovery: if the rest is too short the sprint slows down and the session slides into anaerobic endurance. In the sprints the trainer is in free mode. At most twice a week.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Before the sprints the warm-up prepares your legs; today's goal is waking up the nervous system.
Four minutes left; do not tire yourself now, relax your shoulders before the sprint.

steps.name: Sprint 1
steps.note: Ten seconds at full effort; the first four standing, the rest seated.

steps.name: Rest 1
steps.note: Five minutes of very easy spinning; full recovery is needed.

messages.text: Second sprint; keep your legs turning and do not grip the bars.
You are halfway; the hardest part comes now, keep your exhale strong.
Seven sprints done; in the rest let your breathing calm, the last one comes.
Last sprint, the eighth; give everything now, ten seconds and it is over.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Eight sprints; the nervous system and peak power both got a workout, very well done.

workouts.name: Lead-out sprints 8 × (30 s + 12 s)
workouts.goal: Bringing out a sprint from an already high pace, close to the real finishing situation
workouts.description: Eight repetitions: 30 seconds of 120% “lead-out” pace, then a 12-second sprint brought out at full effort, then five minutes of easy riding. In a race you rarely sprint on fresh legs: before the finish the pace of the bunch is already high. The session imitates that situation, and in the sprint the trainer is in free mode.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Halfway through the warm-up. The point of a lead-out is to start from a high pace, so let your legs get ready.

steps.name: Lead-out 1
steps.note: Thirty seconds at high pace in the wheel.

messages.text: Ten seconds left and the sprint comes. Get ready.

steps.name: Sprint 1
steps.note: Launch at full effort, standing, then push it out.

messages.text: Five minutes of rest. After a lead-out there is always time to breathe; use it.
Halfway through the eight lead-outs. Hold a cadence of 100 for thirty seconds, in the wheel.
Two lead-outs are left. Relax now and bring your heart rate down a little.
The last lead-out: thirty seconds at high pace, then only the last sprint comes.
The last sprint. Start standing, at full effort, then relax.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Eight lead-outs and eight sprints; this is the real finishing situation. Ease off slowly now; that was nice work.

workouts.name: Standing starts 8 × 12 s
workouts.goal: Explosiveness and torque starting from low speed
workouts.description: Eight 12-second sprints from a low cadence (about 50), launched standing in a hard gear; five minutes of easy riding after each. A sprint from a standing start demands the greatest torque, so besides peak power it also develops corner exits and attacks on slow climbs. The trainer is in free mode.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Sprint training is about explosiveness. Let the warm-up prepare your legs.

steps.name: Standing start 1
steps.note: Slow the legs to about 50, hard gear, then explode standing.

steps.name: Rest 1
steps.note: Five minutes of easy riding.

messages.text: The first start is done. Breathe; the heart rate comes down quickly.
Second start done. Sit up straight and relax your thighs.
Take a sip and get ready for the third start; keep your hips stable.
Four starts done, four more come. Hold the hard gear before the start.
Five starts done, three are left. Keep the slowdown before the start controlled.
Six starts done, only two are left. Watch the stability of your hips.
Seven starts done, only the last one is left. Breathe and get ready.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Eight standing starts; very nice force. Slow down now and relax your thighs.

workouts.name: Spun sprints 6 × 15 s
workouts.goal: Seated sprint and fast legs: cadence and neuromuscular coordination
workouts.description: Six 15-second sprints done seated in an easy gear, spun up to the highest cadence possible (120+), with five minutes of rest. The seated, spun sprint trains fast muscle action and coordination; researchers and coaches say it is worth practising next to the standing sprint. The trainer is in free mode.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: The warm-up prepares you for the spins; let your legs stretch out now and the cadence rise slowly.
Four minutes left; think about the high revs now, keep your legs spinning fast.

steps.name: Spin 1
steps.note: Stay seated, easy gear; the revs are the goal, not the watts.

steps.name: Rest 1
steps.note: Five minutes of easy riding.

messages.text: Second spin, stay seated, cadence around 125, legs loose.
Third spin, cadence high, and do not grip the bars.
You are halfway; your legs are tiring, but keep the revs high.
Five spins done; relax now and get ready for the last, sixth spin.
Last spin; keep the revs high and do not slow down at the end.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Six spins; fast legs and coordination improved now, nicely done.

workouts.name: Long climb simulation 60 minutes
workouts.goal: A continuous, long mountain climb at race pace
workouts.description: An hour without interruption, in four fifteen-minute sections with the load rising from 78 to 88%, then a five-minute “finish” near the threshold. The indoor version of an Alpine pass: the long, steady work in the tempo and sweet spot range develops muscular endurance and pacing. Stand up for a minute or two per section, as you would on a real climb.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Today's work simulates a long mountain section. Wake your legs up now and sit loosely in the saddle.

steps.name: Climb 1
steps.note: The bottom of the climb: restrained, seated.

messages.text: Halfway up the first climb. Ride seated, keep the cadence around 80, and do not burn yourself out.
Two minutes left; get ready for the second climb.

steps.name: Climb 2
steps.note: Stand up for a minute in the middle of the section.

messages.text: Halfway through the second section. Keep your breathing deep and your shoulders loose.
Two minutes left; at the end only your strength counts.
Third climb. The speed gets slower, but the watts stay the same. Hold the rhythm.
Halfway; your legs are tired, but keep the cadence around 76, do not let it get too low.

steps.name: Climb 4
steps.note: Hold the pace and the cadence even when tired.

messages.text: Halfway up the last big climb. Sit up straight and watch the rhythm of your breathing.
Two minutes left; now your head decides how long you hold on.

steps.name: Finish to the summit
steps.note: The last five minutes near the threshold.

messages.text: Two and a half minutes to the summit. Get your legs going and do not ease off.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: A long, steady climb; this is real endurance. Bring the pace down slowly now and breathe deeply.

workouts.name: Hill repeats 5 × 3 minutes
workouts.goal: Hill repeats close to VO2max
workouts.description: Five three-minute sections at 108% on an imaginary 5–7% climb, with four minutes of rest. Short, hard climbs load VO2max and strength at once; the slightly lower cadence per repetition (around 75) imitates climbing pedalling. Do one repetition standing.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: For the hill work let your legs wake up; feel the weight on the pedal at the end of the warm-up.

steps.name: Climb 1
steps.note: Three minutes hard at a cadence of about 75; stand up in the last minute.

messages.text: Sit up straight, keep an even momentum, and do not let your back round.
One minute left; your breathing is quick, but keep your legs strong.
Four minutes of rest: sit back in the saddle and take a sip.
Second climb; the cadence is the same, but keep your back firm.
Third climb; you are halfway. Watch the rhythm, not the pain.
Fourth climb; keep your hands and shoulders loose now.
The last climb; this closes the set. Give it everything, then the cool-down.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: After five climbs that was nice work. Slow down now and relax in the saddle.

workouts.name: Torque climbs 4 × 8 minutes (55 rpm)
workouts.goal: Strength endurance and torque at low cadence
workouts.description: Four eight-minute blocks at 85% FTP, at a cadence of about 55, seated. Low-cadence work practises the high-torque pedalling of steep climbs and adds technical variety. Honestly: research (e.g. Kristoffersen et al., 2014) says low cadence on its own improves nothing more than the same work at a natural cadence, so use it as a supplement, not as your main session. Skip it if you have knee or back trouble.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: This torque climb builds strength at a slow cadence; the warm-up now prepares your thighs.
Four minutes left; get ready to pedal slower but with strong pressure.

steps.name: Torque 1
steps.note: Cadence around 55, seated; calm upper body, knee in line.

messages.text: Halfway; sit quietly, do not let your hips rock, let your legs press slowly.

steps.name: Rest 1
steps.note: Rest at a high cadence, around 95: loosen the legs.

messages.text: Spin fast and easily now; the revs are the point in the rest.
Second torque; the slow pace asks for strength again, keep the bars loose.
Halfway up the second climb; keep your shoulders loose and your feet calm.
Third torque; your legs are tired, but keep the cadence around 55.
The last torque; sit up straight, press hard once more at the end, then relax.
One minute left; let your legs press and keep your upper body calm.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Four torque blocks; this was real strength-endurance work, a beautiful performance.

workouts.name: Seated-standing climbing 3 × 12 minutes
workouts.goal: Changing position under load while keeping the watts
workouts.description: Three twelve-minute sweet spot blocks (92% FTP) alternating two minutes seated with one minute standing. On long climbs a change of position rests the muscles, but it only works if the watts do not drop. The session practises that technique while giving valuable sub-threshold work.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Halfway through the warm-up. Today the switch between sitting and standing is the main task, so let your legs loosen up now.

steps.name: Seated 1/1
steps.note: Two minutes seated, cadence around 80.

messages.text: Halfway through the block. The pace is calm; keep your trunk strong.

steps.name: Standing 1/1
steps.note: One minute standing: shift up a gear, keep the watts the same.

messages.text: Half a minute left standing. Sit back down gradually; do not yank the bars.
Five minutes of rest after the first set. Drink and loosen your shoulders.
Two and a half minutes of the rest are left; breathe deeply.
Halfway through the second set. Keep your breathing deep and do not squeeze the bars with your wrists.
Third and last set. The same seated-standing switch, but now on more tired legs.
The last standing effort. The same technique, and do not let the watts drop at the end.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Three sets seated and standing; this is serious fitness. Ease off slowly now and bring your heart rate down.

workouts.name: Short, steep climbs 8 × 90 s
workouts.goal: Force and anaerobic capacity on short, steep walls
workouts.description: Eight ninety-second sections at 120% FTP at a cadence around 70, with three minutes of rest. The short, steep “walls” (classics, hilly sportives) work at the boundary of VO2max and the anaerobic system, with high torque. Alternate one seated and one standing.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Eight short, steep walls come. Spin easily during the warm-up and let your thighs warm up.

steps.name: Wall 1
steps.note: Ninety seconds hard at a cadence around 70; alternate seated and standing.

messages.text: Halfway up the first wall; keep the revs and do not let the rhythm drop.
Three minutes of rest: drink and loosen your wrists.
Second wall; hands on both sides of the bars, keep your hips quiet.
Two walls done, the third comes now; keep your breathing controlled.
Three done, the fourth wall comes now, with a short, sharp effort.
Four walls done, the fifth comes now, and three more after it.
Five done, the sixth wall comes now, two more after it.
Six done, the seventh wall comes. After it only one is left.
The last wall comes. Give everything for a short, sharp effort, then the cool-down.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Eight steep walls; that was nice work. Relax now and stretch a little.

workouts.name: Climbing attacks 4 × 6 minutes
workouts.goal: An attack at the top of the climb after threshold pace
workouts.description: Four six-minute blocks: five minutes at 95% on the climb, then a one-minute attack at 125% before the “summit”, with four minutes of rest. Mountain races are often decided where you have to accelerate once more on tired legs. The session practises that situation.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Today's climbing work is about attacks; the warm-up now prepares your legs.
Five minutes left; set your cadence around 82 before the first climb.

steps.name: Climb 1
steps.note: Five minutes below the threshold, evenly.

messages.text: Halfway; do not let the pace creep up unnoticed, keep your shoulders loose.

steps.name: Attack 1
steps.note: A one-minute attack, launched standing, finished seated.

messages.text: First attack done; in the rest let your breathing calm and your legs loosen.
Second climb; the same pace as at the start, cadence around 82.
Second attack; launch standing, then sit back down, do not lose the rhythm.
Halfway up the climb; keep the pace, do not accelerate too early.
Third attack; keep your exhale strong, then sit down calmly.
Last climb; keep your legs calm now, but strong.
One minute left; get ready for the last attack, breathe deeply.
Last attack; give everything for a minute, then the cool-down.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Four climbs, four attacks; this race-like work was strong, a beautiful performance.

workouts.name: Criterium simulation
workouts.goal: Short, explosive laps and a sprint finish
workouts.description: Six laps, each with a one-minute corner exit at 120%, then four minutes of bunch pace at 88%, and a 30-second finish at the end. It imitates the repeated accelerations of a criterium; the point is that after the jumps you have to be back at a strong pace immediately.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: A criterium is made of short, explosive laps. The warm-up now prepares you for acceleration.

steps.name: Lap 1 – acceleration
steps.note: A corner exit jump: start standing, then sit back down.

messages.text: Half a minute left, then the bunch pace comes. Get ready to sit down.

steps.name: Lap 1 – bunch
steps.note: Four minutes of strong bunch pace; your heart rate is still high.

messages.text: First lap, bunch. Your heart rate is high, so keep your breathing deep and controlled.
Halfway through the bunch pace. Hold the 88% and do not jump ahead of the others.
Halfway through the laps. After the accelerations keep the bunch pace steady.
Sixth acceleration, the last one. Start standing and sit down as soon as your legs find the rhythm.
The last bunch section. Get ready, because the finish follows at the end.

steps.name: Finish
steps.note: The last 30 seconds at full effort.

messages.text: Ten seconds left; bring in all your strength.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Six laps and the finish; you handled this race situation well. Bring your heart rate down slowly.

workouts.name: Attacks and breakaway simulation
workouts.goal: Handling repeated attacks, chases and regrouping
workouts.description: Three attack-chase-regroup blocks, four short accelerations at tempo, three team-work blocks and a one-minute finish. The scenario of a road race: the order and repetition of the different efforts trains what no single interval type can.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: In the bunch, attacks come after the warm-up. Let your legs get ready for short bursts now.

steps.name: Attack 1
steps.note: At full momentum, launched standing.

steps.name: Chase 1
steps.note: A chase at time-trial pace.

messages.text: In the chase sit into the saddle, keep the pace even and your breathing from breaking up.

steps.name: Regroup 1
steps.note: The group comes together: easier, but not resting.

messages.text: An easier section; keep your chest open and your breathing calm.
Second chase; the pace is the same as the first. Do not skip the breathing.
Third attack. Show what you can do in a short, sharper burst.
We are in the middle of the chase; keep the cadence around 90.

steps.name: Acceleration 1
steps.note: A short acceleration, then back to tempo.

messages.text: Back to tempo after the acceleration. Do not let your legs slow down; keep your breathing calm.
Halfway through the tempo; keep the revs and drop your shoulders.

steps.name: Turn on the front 1
steps.note: A turn on the front, hard.

messages.text: You are resting in the wheel now, but watch your heart rate; the next turn comes soon.

steps.name: Finale
steps.note: A long finish, the last 15 seconds at full effort.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Nice work in the bunch: attack, chase, regroup. Slow down now and drink water.

workouts.name: Pre-race activation (opener)
workouts.goal: Waking the nervous system up the day before a race, without fatigue
workouts.description: A short, sharp opener session for the day before a race: three half-minute accelerations, a short FTP block and two ten-second sprints, with plenty of easy riding. The aim is to wake the legs and recall race pace, not to tire you; you should feel fresh at the end.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A calm build-up; no need to hurry.

messages.text: Today's session is about waking the nervous system; the warm-up now loosens your legs.
Five minutes, then the short accelerations come; keep the cadence high and your breathing calm.

steps.name: Acceleration 1
steps.note: About a 90% effort, not full; the aim is waking up.

messages.text: Second acceleration, the same wake-up effort, no more than needed.
The last acceleration in the set; cadence around 110, then ease off.

steps.name: FTP block
steps.note: Two and a half minutes at FTP, recalling race pace.

messages.text: Halfway; let your legs remember the pace and keep your breathing deep.

steps.name: Sprint 1
steps.note: Ten seconds sharply.

messages.text: Rest before the second sprint; let your breathing settle and get ready.
The last ten seconds, sharply, then the opener is over.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Your nervous system is awake now; this preparation will help in tomorrow's race.

workouts.name: Quick activation 30 minutes
workouts.goal: A short opener on race day or before it, when time is short
workouts.description: Half an hour: warm-up, three one-minute lifts near the threshold and three short sprints. Following the pattern of pre-race warm-ups, it prepares the cardiovascular system and the muscles for the start without tiring them. It can also serve as a warm-up before short races (crit, time trial).

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: This short opener prepares the sharp state. Wake your legs up slowly now.

steps.name: Lift 1
steps.note: One minute at FTP, controlled.

messages.text: Thirty seconds left; keep the cadence at 95 and your shoulders loose.
Second lift. After the first you know how much you need to hold the watts.
The last lift at FTP; after it only the short sprints come.

steps.name: Sprint 1
steps.note: Eight seconds sharply.

messages.text: Second sprint, short and sharp. Just steer your breathing.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Three lifts and three sprints; this short session was serious work too. Ease off slowly and look back satisfied.

workouts.name: Time-trial simulation 40 minutes
workouts.goal: Time-trial pacing: a restrained start, a strong finish
workouts.description: Forty minutes of time-trial pace in three sections: ten minutes at 95%, twenty at 98%, then ten at 100–103% with the last two minutes a free finale. Time trials are most often ruined by starting too fast; the session teaches negative-split pacing. If you have a time-trial position, ride in it.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Today's task is the restrained start and the strong end. Keep the patience in the warm-up.

steps.name: Opening 1
steps.note: Two short lifts before the start.

messages.text: A short pause before the start. Take a sip and calm your breathing.
Second short lift, then the start comes. Do not spend energy now.
One minute to the start. Take a deep breath, keep your shoulders loose.

steps.name: Start – restrained
steps.note: The first ten minutes should feel too easy. Good.

messages.text: Do not watch the others, just hold your 95% pace; you will need the strength at the end.

steps.name: Middle section
steps.note: Steady, in position; watch only the next minute.

messages.text: Halfway through the middle section: hold your position, do not watch the speed.
Last minute of the middle section; the strong finish is close.

steps.name: Strong finish
steps.note: Lift; from here you do not need to save anything.

messages.text: Halfway through the finish; make the revs quicker and keep your hips stable.

steps.name: Finish
steps.note: The last two minutes are free: push out whatever is left.

messages.text: One more minute; give out everything you have been saving.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: The time-trial simulation is done; that was nice work with the restrained start and the strong finish. Slow down.

workouts.name: Breakaway simulation 3 × (1 + 8 minutes)
workouts.goal: Holding the breakaway near the threshold after an attack
workouts.description: Three blocks: a one-minute attack at 130%, then straight into eight minutes at 95%, with five minutes of rest. A breakaway is not decided by the attack but by holding the following minutes while the lactate is still high. This session practises exactly that painful transition.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: The breakaway simulation is about holding after the attack; the warm-up now prepares your legs.
Five minutes left; get ready, because after the first attack you cannot ease off.

steps.name: Attack 1
steps.note: One minute at full momentum, to get away.

steps.name: Hold 1
steps.note: Straight back to 95%: the first two minutes are the hardest, do not give in.

messages.text: Halfway through the breakaway; keep your hips quiet and the cadence around 90.
One minute left; do not let the pace go, the bunch will not catch you now.
First breakaway done; in the rest let your breathing settle, the second attack comes.
Second attack; start hard, then settle back to the same pace.
Halfway through the second breakaway; keep the pace around 95 and do not let your legs relax.
Last attack; give everything for a minute, then hold the pace.
The last hold; your goal is clear, keep your exhale strong.
One minute left; do not slow down at the end, because that is the point of a breakaway.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Three attacks, three holds; the breakaway simulation builds staying power, nice work.

workouts.name: Gravel and MTB: a varying load
workouts.goal: A constantly changing load, as on the terrain
workouts.description: Three blocks, each alternating short, steep ramps (30 s at 140%), tempo straights and climbs around the threshold, without rest. Gravel and MTB loads are rarely even: many short accelerations with almost no rest between. The session loads VO2max, anaerobic capacity and the ability to pick the pace up again all at once.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Today's varied terrain: gravel and hills. Feel the rhythm of the wheels during the warm-up.

steps.name: Climb 1
steps.note: Three minutes at the threshold, like a longer hill.

messages.text: Halfway up the hill. Ride seated, keep the cadence around 80 and breathe calmly.

steps.name: Ramp 1
steps.note: A short, steep ramp: standing, hard.

steps.name: Straight 1
steps.note: Tempo on the gravel; not a rest.

messages.text: Ninety seconds left; hold the 80% and do not let go of the bars.
A rolling section: the watts rise and fall. Keep your breathing even.
A straight at 78%. Not a rest, just even tempo, so you still have strength for the next hill.
One minute left of the straight; get ready for the rest.
Five minutes of rest after the first section. Drink and relax your hands.
The second hill. Start seated the same way and keep the cadence at 80.
Halfway through the second straight. Your heart rate is high, but keep the watts the same.
Second rest, before the third hill. Breathe deeply and relax.
Third hill. Sit, breathe, and keep your shoulders and hands loose.
One minute left of the last straight; give a little more at the end.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: After the gravel, the hills and the straights you can finally relax. Bring your heart rate down slowly; nice work.

workouts.name: Group ride simulation 90 minutes
workouts.goal: Bunch-like, rolling load: aerobic base with changes of rhythm
workouts.description: An hour and a half of zone 2 and 3 with irregular accelerations (15 s–1 minute, 105–150%), as on a group ride or at the start of an amateur race. Useful when you have no group: it gives an aerobic base while practising changes of rhythm. Not a key session, more a quality “long ride”.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: In the bunch, after the warm-up your legs prepare for the rolling; keep the pedal light.

steps.name: Acceleration 1
steps.note: Someone went off the front: close it, then back to tempo.

steps.name: Bunch 1
steps.note: Bunch pace at the boundary of zones 2 and 3.

messages.text: Find the group's rhythm; do not follow the others' momentum blindly.
Bunch pace again. Keep your position stable and your hands loose on the bars.
Almost three minutes more; let your breathing start to slow.
Halfway through the third bunch: do not let your legs slow their turning.
The middle of this bunch. Keep your breathing calm and your shoulders loose.
A short bunch follows. Hold the 68% until the next acceleration comes.
The pace is familiar by now, but keep watching the cadence.
Halfway through the seventh bunch. Keep your hips stable and look ahead.
The last bunch comes; watch the cadence, then the easy part follows.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: You held your place in the bunch all the way, even after many accelerations. Nice work; relax now.

workouts.name: FTP test 20 minutes (with a 5-minute opener)
workouts.goal: Determining FTP with Hunter Allen's twenty-minute protocol
workouts.description: A thorough warm-up, three spins, a five-minute maximal effort, then after ten minutes of rest the 20-minute test. FTP is 95% of the 20-minute average power; the five-minute effort before it takes the edge off your freshness, so the 20-minute number lands closer to hour power. In the test sections the trainer is in free mode: you pace. After the test the Review → Power page offers the new FTP from your best 20 minutes (calculated from measured watts only).

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: This is the FTP test; today's goal is an accurate measurement, and the warm-up now prepares your legs.
Ten minutes left; keep your breathing calm and the cadence around 85.
Two minutes and the first short wake-up comes; do not tire yourself beforehand.

steps.name: Spin 1
steps.note: Fast legs, above 110.

messages.text: Last spin before the opener; keep the revs high, then rest.
The short, strong opener comes now; in the rest let your breathing settle.

steps.name: 5 minutes maximal
steps.note: Hard, but not to complete exhaustion; this is the opener.

messages.text: Halfway; sit down and hold an even force, do not accelerate too early.
Five minutes left; let your breathing calm, and take a sip before the main test.

steps.name: 20-minute test
steps.note: Start restrained, lift in the second ten minutes; the last two minutes at full effort.

messages.text: Five minutes in; check now that the pace is even.
Halfway; sit up straight, keep your breathing deep and the cadence around 90.
One minute left; put every last bit in.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: You did the FTP test; the numbers now point the way for your training. Nice work.

workouts.name: FTP test 2 × 8 minutes (CTS)
workouts.goal: Estimating FTP with two eight-minute efforts
workouts.description: Two eight-minute maximal efforts with ten minutes of rest. Shorter sections are easier to pace well, so it is more reliable than the twenty-minute test for beginners too; FTP is estimated as about 90% of the better of the two 8-minute averages. In the test sections the trainer is in free mode.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Halfway through the warm-up. Today's test builds on estimating FTP; do not tire yourself now.
Two minutes left of the warm-up; get ready for the short spins.

steps.name: Spin 1
steps.note: Fast legs, above 110.

messages.text: Half a minute left, then the rest comes. Breathe deeply and keep your legs turning.
Second short spin. This is the last sharp moment of the warm-up; just let your legs spin.
Two and a half minutes left of the rest. Breathe deeply; before the test the heart rate has to come down.

steps.name: 1st eight minutes
steps.note: A strong, even start; give everything in the last minute.

messages.text: Halfway through the first eight minutes. Hold the starting strength and keep your breathing deep and even.
One minute left of the first test; keep the cadence around 92.
Five minutes to the second test. Get ready, but do not ride too hard.

steps.name: 2nd eight minutes
steps.note: The same strategy; it is good if this one is not weaker than the first.

messages.text: Halfway. Keep the same pace as the first and your breathing steady.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Two eight-minute efforts; this is the basis of your FTP estimate. Bring your heart rate down slowly; nice work.

workouts.name: Ramp test 20 W/min
workouts.goal: A quick determination of maximal aerobic power and estimated FTP
workouts.description: After a short warm-up, the load rises by 20 watts a minute to complete exhaustion in ERG mode. About 75% of the last complete minute's average gives the FTP estimate. Short, easy to repeat, with little room for pacing error; for the average rider this is the default test. Stop when you can no longer hold the cadence.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: The ramp test is about the gradual rise; do not tire yourself yet.

steps.name: Tuning in
steps.note: Three minutes steady, then the steps start.

messages.text: A minute and a half to the test; fix your position now.

steps.name: Ramp
steps.note: Plus 20 W every minute. Hold the cadence as long as you can; when it is gone, the test is over.

messages.text: You are in the middle of the test; keep your breathing deep and even.
When you can no longer hold the steps, do not force it; the real data is what matters.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: The test is done; that was nice work. Slow down now and relax your shoulders.

workouts.name: Ramp test 15 W/min (fine steps)
workouts.goal: A more precise MAP estimate with smaller steps, for easier riders
workouts.description: Steps rising by 15 watts a minute to exhaustion. The smaller step gives a more accurate result at a lower FTP (below about 200 W), because the test lasts over more steps. The FTP estimate here is again about 75% of the last complete minute.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: This is a fine ramp test; the warm-up now prepares your legs for the gradual rise.
Three minutes left; get ready, the ramp starts soon.

steps.name: Tuning in
steps.note: Two minutes steady.

messages.text: A little momentum before the ramp; keep the cadence around 95 and your legs turning.

steps.name: Ramp
steps.note: Plus 15 W every minute, to exhaustion.

messages.text: Fifth minute; keep your breathing rhythmic and the cadence around 90.
Ten minutes; keep your upper body loose and your hands from tensing on the bars.
About five minutes more; watch your breathing and do not fall out of the rhythm.
One minute left; if you cannot hold it, slow down calmly, you still get the test result.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Your measured result is a good basis for the coming sessions now; nice work.

workouts.name: Ramp test 25 W/min
workouts.goal: A quicker ramp test for stronger riders
workouts.description: Steps rising by 25 watts a minute to exhaustion, at a higher FTP (above about 300 W), so the test does not become too long. The shorter test is less tiring, so maximal aerobic power can be measured more accurately. The FTP estimate is about 75% of the last complete minute.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: This ramp test is for stronger riders; the warm-up is the key now. Get your heart rate up already.

steps.name: Tuning in
steps.note: Three minutes steady.

messages.text: Three minutes steady, keep the cadence at 95. This is the last calm section before the test.

steps.name: Ramp
steps.note: Plus 25 W every minute, to exhaustion.

messages.text: We raise 25 watts every minute. It is still easy at the start, but the cadence will be the signal at the end.
Five minutes of the ramp have passed. Do not watch the watts, watch your breathing and your cadence.
If you can no longer hold the cadence, slow down calmly; that is part of the test too.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: A hard ramp test that gives a lot of information about your fitness. Ease off slowly now and look back proudly.

workouts.name: MAP test with 3-minute steps
workouts.goal: Steady-state maximal aerobic power with longer steps
workouts.description: Three-minute, 30-watt steps to exhaustion. In the longer steps oxygen uptake and heart rate can settle, so it is closer to the classic MAP protocol used in laboratories, and it can also be used to set heart rate zones. Longer and harder than a per-minute ramp.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: The warm-up now prepares your head. Today brings steady, longer steps.

steps.name: Tuning in
steps.note: Three minutes steady.

messages.text: Halfway through the tuning in. Sit up straight and keep the cadence around 95.

steps.name: Stepped test
steps.note: Three-minute steps, +30 W; watch your heart rate at the end of every step.

messages.text: Two steps done, the third comes. Keep your breathing even.
It is noticeably harder now; keep your shoulders loose and your hips stable.
Two more minutes of the test; hold the revs as long as you can.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: The stepped test is done; good work. Ride on slowly now and relax your hands.

workouts.name: Critical power test 3 + 12 minutes
workouts.goal: Estimating critical power (CP) and the anaerobic reserve (W′)
workouts.description: A three-minute and a twelve-minute maximal effort, with thirty minutes of easy riding between them. From the two average powers, critical power (a good approximation of the threshold) and W′, that is, how much work you can do above the threshold, can be calculated. According to Karsten et al., multi-point field CP tests are valid and reliable. Both sections in free mode, evenly paced.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: The CP test has two parts; the warm-up now prepares your legs and your breathing.
Ten minutes left; before the first opener keep the cadence around 90.
Two minutes and the first one-minute wake-up comes; cadence around 100.

steps.name: Opening 1
steps.note: One minute at FTP, a wake-up.

messages.text: One minute of rest; let your breathing calm, then the second short wake-up comes.
Second wake-up, harder now, but keep the cadence at 100; then the opening is over.
Four minutes before the start; loosen your shoulders, the three-minute test comes.
Two minutes left; get ready for the three-minute maximum, do not waste it.

steps.name: 3 minutes maximal
steps.note: Evenly, and give everything in the last minute.

messages.text: Halfway; keep the cadence around 100 and do not slow down on the exhale.

steps.name: Rest
steps.note: Thirty minutes of easy riding; do not shorten it.

messages.text: Ten minutes of rest; let your legs loosen and drink, so you have strength for the twelve-minute test.
Five minutes left; your heart rate has come down; get ready to focus.

steps.name: 12 minutes maximal
steps.note: A restrained first three minutes, then lift.

messages.text: Halfway; the pace is still holdable, your breathing calm and your head clear.
One minute left; now you need all your strength, come on.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: The CP test is done; the numbers now give you your zones too. Nice work.

workouts.name: Power profile test (15 s, 1 minute, 5 minutes)
workouts.goal: Mapping strengths and weaknesses for the power profile
workouts.description: A 15-second sprint (the best 5 seconds count), a one-minute and a five-minute maximal effort, with generous rests. Allen and Coggan's power profile compares these numbers (together with the 20-minute FTP test) to reveal whether you are a sprinter, an all-rounder or a time-triallist, and where your biggest reserve is. Every test section in free mode.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Halfway through the warm-up. Today's test measures three short sections; let your legs and your breathing get ready.
Three minutes left of the warm-up; only easy spinning from here.

steps.name: Wake-up 1
steps.note: A short, light acceleration.

messages.text: A short rest before the next acceleration. Relax and breathe deeply.
Four minutes of rest before the sprint. Ride calmly and get ready for the strongest start.
Two minutes left; do not let your legs go cold.

steps.name: 15 s sprint
steps.note: At full effort, launched standing.

messages.text: Ten minutes of rest; drink and breathe, so the one-minute test is clean.
Five minutes left of the first rest; get ready for the one-minute maximum.

steps.name: 1 minute maximal
steps.note: A strong start, but hold it all the way.

messages.text: Half a minute left; keep your breathing deep and even.
Now fifteen minutes of rest before the five-minute test. Drink and relax.
Five minutes left of the rest; get ready for the five-minute test.

steps.name: 5 minutes maximal
steps.note: Even pacing, give everything in the last minute.

messages.text: Halfway through the five-minute test. Hold the pace and do not accelerate suddenly.
Thirty seconds more; give what is left, then it is over.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: That was the full profile: short, medium and longer efforts. Ease off slowly now; very good work.

workouts.name: Durability test: 5 minutes after 90 minutes
workouts.goal: How much your power drops after a long load
workouts.description: After ninety minutes at 75% FTP, a five-minute maximal effort. Compare it with a five-minute result measured fresh and rested: the difference is your durability. Research says tired-state performance counts separately for amateurs too, and successful riders fade less.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: This test is about endurance; during the warm-up wake your legs up easily.

steps.name: Preload 1
steps.note: Steady 75%, regular eating and drinking.

messages.text: Ten minutes have passed; the 75% should be comfortable and your breathing calm.
Halfway: a little snack helps now; the second half is still long.
Two more minutes, then the second dose comes.

steps.name: Preload 2
steps.note: The same; do not speed up before the test.

messages.text: The second dose comes now; the fatigue is normal, keep the watts.
Halfway through the second part. Take a few sips and loosen your hands.
Last minute of the preload; get ready for the short rest and the test.
Three minutes of rest before the test. Relax, drink, and calm your breathing.

steps.name: 5 minutes maximal when tired
steps.note: Even pacing, as if you were fresh.

messages.text: Halfway through the five minutes; keep your hips quiet and your shoulders loose.
Thirty seconds more; everything into the revs.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: The test is done; that was very strong work. Ride on slowly now and let the air out.

workouts.name: Threshold and VO2max combo
workouts.goal: Two key stimuli in one session: threshold, then VO2max
workouts.description: Two twelve-minute threshold blocks (97%), then five two-minute VO2max repetitions (118%). After the threshold work you have to work in the high aerobic range already tired, which is typical of the second half of races. For advanced riders, when you have to pack a lot of quality into few key sessions a week.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Today's session has two big parts; the warm-up now prepares you for the threshold.
Five minutes left; before the threshold keep your breathing deep and calm.

steps.name: Threshold 1
steps.note: A hair below FTP, evenly.

messages.text: Halfway; keep the cadence around 90 and your exhale long.
Two minutes left; hold the pace and do not ease off at the end.
First threshold done; in the rest loosen your shoulders, the second threshold comes.
Second threshold, now on more tired legs, but keep the pace the same.
Four minutes left of the threshold; keep your breathing rhythmic.

steps.name: VO2max 1
steps.note: Two minutes hard, on tired legs too.

messages.text: First short VO2max section; cadence around 102, exhale strong.
Second round; the fatigue shows now, but keep the pace around 118.
Halfway through the VO2max part; keep your legs fast and your upper body calm.
Fourth round; keep your breathing strong and do not let the cadence drop.
Last round; everything into the cadence, and a little more staying power at the end.
One minute left; keep the exhale to the end, then the cool-down comes.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: You did two different kinds of work, threshold and VO2max both; this is real staying power.

workouts.name: Sweet spot and tired sprints
workouts.goal: Sweet spot work, then sprints on tired legs, as at the end of a race
workouts.description: Three twelve-minute sweet spot blocks, then four 10-second sprints with five minutes of rest. At the end of a race you have to sprint without fresh legs: the tired sprint is a separate ability. In the sprints the trainer is in free mode.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Halfway through the warm-up. Today's session is about tired sprints, so do not waste your legs.

steps.name: Sweet spot 1
steps.note: 90%, evenly.

messages.text: Halfway through the first sweet spot. Keep your breathing deep and your shoulders loose.
Two minutes left of the first block; get ready for the rest.
Four minutes of rest. Relax your hands and take a sip.
Second sweet spot, at 90%. The fatigue shows after the first block, but keep the watts.
Four minutes left of this block; keep the cadence around 90.
Third sweet spot block, the last before the main work. Now discipline is what matters.
Four minutes left. Sprints come at the end, so your legs still have to hold.
Five minutes of rest; after this the tired sprints come. Breathe deeply and relax.

steps.name: Tired sprint 1
steps.note: At full effort, launched standing.

messages.text: Second tired sprint. Your legs are heavy now, but the initial impulse is what matters.
Third sprint. This fatigue imitates the end of a race, so do not give up.
The second-to-last rest, then the last sprint comes. Use the breathing.
Last sprint. Start standing, at full effort; after it only the cool-down.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: Three sweet spot blocks and four sprints; today's work is a real milestone. Bring your heart rate down slowly.

workouts.name: Long base with a VO2max finish 2 hours
workouts.goal: Durability: VO2max work after an hour of load
workouts.description: After seventy-five minutes of zone 2, four three-minute VO2max repetitions (112%), then a cool-down. The high intensity after a long preload develops aerobic capacity and durability at once; the decisive moments of races arrive the same way. Only with a good base, and plenty of carbohydrate.

steps.name: Warm-up
steps.note: A gradual build-up; at the end, two or three short, loose accelerations above 100 rpm.

messages.text: Today's work is two hours. After the warm-up let the pace be comfortable, not hurried.

steps.name: Zone 2 – 1
steps.note: Steady; eat regularly.

messages.text: Now the long base is what matters: even cadence, calm shoulders.
Halfway through the base. Take a sip and watch how deep your breathing is.
One more minute of the base; get ready for the transition.
Second base block; the pace is a little stronger now. Do not let your hands tense.
Halfway through the second base block; the fatigue comes now, keep your form.
Last minute of the base; keep the cadence, because the VO2max part follows.
Three minutes of transition; let your legs gather themselves for the VO2max.

steps.name: Tired VO2max 1
steps.note: Tired legs have to hold the same wattage.

messages.text: You are halfway; keep the revs strong but do not let your breathing fall apart.
Second tired interval; use your head now, the revs are the same.
Third tired interval; your legs may feel heavy. Sit up straight and keep your collarbone relaxed.
Last VO2max, give it everything; after it only the cool-down is left.

steps.name: Cool-down
steps.note: An easy spin; let your heart rate come down slowly.

messages.text: That was two hours of work; you held the VO2max even when tired. Very nice work; relax now.
